questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 1 item 2(3). Emergency first aid means the immediate measures needed to help an injured person at the scene of a traffic accident.
questions.question: As a precaution you should take out motor insurance, learn what you need to know for emergency first aid, and keep first-aid equipment in the vehicle.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 1 item 1. Keeping them is treated as a basic duty of a member of society.
questions.question: Traffic rules are set as the common promises everyone must keep so that all can use the road safely and smoothly.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 1 item 2(5). It is not a rule for drivers alone.
questions.question: Pedestrians and cyclists also need a good understanding of what cars are like, including blind spots and the inner wheel difference.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 1 item 2(7). Nobody being nearby does not make it something you can ignore.
questions.question: Bear in mind that the person operating a remotely operated small vehicle may not be nearby and that it may stop suddenly on the road.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 1 item 2(5) pedestrians and people riding specified small motorized bicycles and bicycles are to know about them too.
questions.question: Only drivers of cars need to know about blind spots and the inner wheel difference.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 1 item 1 they are the common promises everyone must keep so that all can use the road safely and smoothly.
questions.question: Traffic rules are made only for congested places and need not be kept on a quiet road.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 1 item 2(6) you need to know that automated vehicles may be used with the driver not watching the road ahead.
questions.question: Because an automated driving device drives an automated vehicle, its driver is never not watching the road ahead.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 1 item 2(7) that person may not be nearby.
questions.question: The person operating a remotely operated small vehicle is always nearby.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 1 item 2(8). Chapter 1 Section 4 sets out concrete prohibitions to the same effect.
questions.question: You must not throw things away on the road or leave things there without permission, since it obstructs and inconveniences other people.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). A general motorized bicycle (moped) making a two-step right turn is treated separately.
questions.question: On a green light, vehicles other than specified small motorized bicycles and light road vehicles may go straight on, turn left and turn right.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). Even on green it cannot complete the right turn in one movement.
questions.question: Even on a green light, a general motorized bicycle (moped) making a two-step right turn may only go straight to the turning point and change direction there.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). Where there is a stop line, the stopping position is just before it.
questions.question: On a red light a vehicle or streetcar (tram) must not proceed beyond the stopping position.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). The rule keeps a vehicle that has already entered and begun its turn from stopping midway.
questions.question: A vehicle already turning left at an intersection may carry on even if the light for the direction it is turning into is red.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). It may proceed, but that does not give it priority.
questions.question: A vehicle already turning right at an intersection may carry on even if the light for that direction is red, but it must not obstruct vehicles coming through on a green light.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). Specified small motorized bicycles and light road vehicles are treated the same way.
questions.question: A general motorized bicycle (moped) making a two-step right turn must wait at the turning point while the light for that direction is red.

questions.explanation: This is the note to Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). Where there is no stop line, the stopping position is defined for each kind of place.
questions.question: The stopping position is the point just before the stop line where there is one.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(1) a vehicle must not proceed beyond the stopping position on a red light.
questions.question: On a red light a vehicle must proceed slowly (徐行) just before the stopping position.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(1) it must still not obstruct vehicles or streetcars (trams) coming through on a green light.
questions.question: A vehicle already turning right at an intersection may simply carry on once the light for that direction is red.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(1) a vehicle that was close to the stopping position when the light changed and cannot stop safely may carry on.
questions.question: On an amber light a vehicle must never proceed beyond the stopping position, in any circumstances.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under the note to Kyosoku Appendix 1(1) it is just before the intersection at an intersection, and just before a pedestrian crossing or railway crossing where one lies outside an intersection.
questions.question: Where there is no stop line, the stopping position is the point just before the traffic light.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(1) a pedestrian may go on a green light. It is on an amber light that they must not begin crossing.
questions.question: On a green light a pedestrian must not begin crossing.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(1) a vehicle already turning may proceed, but it must not obstruct vehicles coming through on a green light.
questions.question: At an intersection on a red light, a vehicle midway through a right turn may go ahead of oncoming vehicles coming through on a green light.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(1), if you can stop safely you must not proceed beyond the stopping position.
questions.question: The light ahead turned amber but you were still some way from the stopping position, so you accelerated into the intersection.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(1) it may go straight on and turn left, and turns right by going straight to the turning point and changing direction there.
questions.question: A specified small motorized bicycle may go straight on, turn left and turn right on a green light.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). The arrow permits movement only in the direction it points.
questions.question: On a green arrow light a vehicle may go in the direction of the arrow even though the light is amber or red.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). This applies to the right-pointing arrow alone.
questions.question: When a right-pointing green arrow is shown, a vehicle may also make a U-turn.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). Specified small motorized bicycles and light road vehicles are treated the same way.
questions.question: Where the green arrow points right, a general motorized bicycle (moped) making a two-step right turn may not go in the direction of the arrow.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). The yellow arrow is addressed to streetcars alone.
questions.question: On a yellow arrow light a streetcar (tram) may go in the direction of the arrow, but pedestrians and vehicles must not proceed.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). Pedestrians may likewise proceed with care for other traffic.
questions.question: On a flashing yellow light a vehicle or streetcar (tram) may proceed with care for other traffic.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). After stopping you proceed once you have checked that it is safe.
questions.question: On a flashing red light a vehicle or streetcar (tram) must come to a complete stop (一時停止) at the stopping position.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). It is vehicles and streetcars (trams) that must come to a complete stop (一時停止).
questions.question: On a flashing red light a pedestrian may proceed with care for other traffic.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). A pedestrian who has not yet started must not begin crossing.
questions.question: On a flashing green light with a figure symbol, a pedestrian already crossing must finish promptly or give up and turn back.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(2). To turn right they go straight to the turning point and change direction there.
questions.question: On a light marked Pedestrians and bicycles only, the green light with a figure symbol lets a specified small motorized bicycle and a bicycle go straight on and turn left.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). Pedestrians must not cross.
questions.question: On a red light with a figure symbol, an ordinary bicycle about to use the pedestrian crossing must not begin crossing.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(1) a vehicle must come to a complete stop (一時停止) at the stopping position on a flashing red light.
questions.question: On a flashing red light a vehicle may proceed with care for other traffic.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(1) you may proceed with care for other traffic on a flashing yellow light.
questions.question: On a flashing yellow light a vehicle must come to a complete stop (一時停止) at the stopping position.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(1) only a streetcar (tram) may go in the direction of a yellow arrow.
questions.question: On a yellow arrow light a vehicle may also go in the direction of the arrow.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(1), where the arrow points right, specified small motorized bicycles, light road vehicles and mopeds making a two-step right turn may not go.
questions.question: On a green arrow light every vehicle may go in the direction of the arrow.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(1) a U-turn is also permitted where the arrow points right.
questions.question: Even when a right-pointing green arrow is shown, a vehicle may not make a U-turn.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. After stopping you must check that it is safe, and you must not obstruct the progress of vehicles on the crossing road (Road Traffic Act Article 43).
questions.question: On a flashing red light you may go ahead of vehicles on the crossing road as long as you have come to a complete stop (一時停止) at the stopping position.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(2), where the light is marked Pedestrians and bicycles only, specified small motorized bicycles and bicycles must follow it too.
questions.question: A light with a figure symbol is addressed to pedestrians, so a bicycle never has to follow it.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(1) you may go only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.question: When a green arrow is shown you may also go in directions other than the arrow.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(1) you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) at the stopping position on a flashing red light.
questions.question: The light ahead was flashing red, but you only slowed down and went through because you saw no vehicles on the crossing road.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(2), a bicycle that was close to the stopping position when it began flashing and cannot stop safely may carry on.
questions.question: Where the light marked Pedestrians and bicycles only shows a flashing green with a figure symbol, a bicycle must not begin crossing.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 1(2). Some lights turn red in every direction for a moment.
questions.question: Watch the light ahead of you, and bear in mind that the light ahead is not necessarily green just because the one to the side has turned red.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 1(2). That is exactly why you watch the light ahead rather than the one to the side.
questions.question: Some lights, such as staggered-phase signals, delay the moment when the light for one particular direction turns red.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 1(3). Where a light is specified for particular vehicles or pedestrians, you follow that specified light.
questions.question: A light carrying a plate such as Buses only is addressed to the vehicles named on that plate.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 1(4). The plate is the Left turn permitted sign in Kyosoku Appendix 2(2).
questions.question: Where a plate with a blue left-pointing arrow on white stands at the left edge of the road or on the signal, a vehicle may turn left with care for the surrounding traffic even though the light ahead is red or amber.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 1(4). You may turn, but that does not give you priority.
questions.question: When you turn left on the strength of the left-arrow plate, you must not obstruct pedestrians or bicycles crossing on the signal.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 2(1). Main signs divide further into four kinds.
questions.question: A road sign is a plate showing a traffic regulation or the like, and there are main signs and auxiliary signs.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 2(1). What each one means is set out in Kyosoku Appendix 3(1).
questions.question: There are four kinds of main road sign: regulatory, indication, warning and guide signs.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 2(2). The sign closing a road to cars and the sign setting a maximum speed are examples.
questions.question: A regulatory sign prohibits a particular way of using the road or specifies that you travel in a particular way.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 2(4). The sign showing a railway crossing ahead is an example.
questions.question: A warning sign gives road users advance notice of a danger or a situation on the road that calls for care.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 2(6). Abbreviations such as those in Kyosoku Appendix 4 are sometimes used to name vehicle types.
questions.question: An auxiliary sign is normally fitted below the main sign and states the reason for the restriction or specifies the times, days or vehicle types it applies to.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 1(2) some lights turn red in every direction and some are staggered-phase, so you must watch the light ahead.
questions.question: When the light to the side turns red, the light ahead is bound to turn green.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 2(3) an indication sign shows that a particular way of using the road is allowed, or marks a place fixed by traffic law.
questions.question: An indication sign prohibits a particular way of using the road or specifies that you travel in a particular way.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 2(5) a guide sign shows place names, directions and distances to make travelling easier.
questions.question: A guide sign gives advance notice of a danger or a situation on the road that calls for care.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 2(1) there is also the guide sign, making four kinds.
questions.question: There are three kinds of main road sign: regulatory, indication and warning signs.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 1(4) you must not obstruct pedestrians crossing on the signal.
questions.question: Where the left-arrow plate stands you may turn left ahead of pedestrians in the middle of crossing, even on a red light.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 1(4) the plate permits a left turn only.
questions.question: Where the left-arrow plate stands a vehicle may also go straight on even though the light ahead is red.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 1(3) that light is addressed to the vehicles named on the plate, and other vehicles follow the ordinary light.
questions.question: A light carrying a Buses only plate must be obeyed by vehicles other than route buses as well.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 2(6) it is normally fitted below the main sign and also specifies times, days and vehicle types.
questions.question: An auxiliary sign is normally fitted above the main sign and states the reason for the restriction and nothing else.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 2(1) road signs comprise main signs and auxiliary signs.
questions.question: A road sign means the main sign, and auxiliary signs are not counted as road signs.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 1(4), even when turning on that plate you must not obstruct pedestrians crossing on the signal.
questions.question: The light ahead was red, but because a left-arrow plate stood at the left edge of the road you turned left across in front of pedestrians who were crossing.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 3(1). They are distinct from road signs, which are plates set up beside the road.
questions.question: Road markings are the lines, symbols and characters shown on the road surface in paint, road studs and the like, and there are two kinds: regulatory and indication markings.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 3(2). The marking prohibiting parking and the one designating a bus lane are examples.
questions.question: A regulatory marking is one that prohibits or specifies a particular way of using the road.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 3(2). The marking showing that diagonal crossing is allowed and the one showing where vehicles stop are examples.
questions.question: An indication marking is one that shows that a particular way of using the road is allowed, or marks a place fixed by traffic law.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). Specified small motorized bicycles and light road vehicles are treated differently.
questions.question: On a green light a streetcar (tram) may go straight on, turn left and turn right.

questions.explanation: This is the note to Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). Where a pedestrian crossing or bicycle crossing lies right by the intersection, it is just before that.
questions.question: At an intersection with no stop line, the stopping position is just before the intersection.

questions.explanation: This is the note to Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). Where there is a stop line, the stopping position is just before it.
questions.question: Where a traffic light stands outside an intersection at a place with no pedestrian crossing, bicycle crossing or railway crossing, the stopping position is just before the light.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 2(3). The sign showing that parking is allowed and the signs marking a pedestrian crossing or safety zone are examples.
questions.question: An indication sign shows that a particular way of using the road is allowed, or marks a place fixed by traffic law.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 2(6). The abbreviations are collected in Kyosoku Appendix 4.
questions.question: Abbreviations are sometimes used on an auxiliary sign when it names the types of vehicle and in similar cases.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). The case where it was close to that position when the light changed and cannot stop safely is an exception.
questions.question: On an amber light a streetcar (tram) must not proceed beyond the stopping position either.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). Vehicles are treated the same way.
questions.question: A streetcar (tram) already turning left at an intersection may carry on even if the light for that direction is red.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 3(2) a regulatory marking prohibits or specifies a way of using the road; showing what is allowed is the indication marking.
questions.question: A regulatory marking is one that shows that a particular way of using the road is allowed.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 3(1) road markings are the lines, symbols and characters shown on the road surface in paint, road studs and the like.
questions.question: Road markings mean only those shown in paint; ones made with road studs are not included.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(1) a streetcar may go straight on, turn left and turn right on a green light.
questions.question: On a green light a streetcar (tram) may only go straight on and turn left.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under the note to Kyosoku Appendix 1(1) it is just before the intersection.
questions.question: At an intersection with no stop line, the stopping position is the centre of the intersection.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 2(3) it is given as an example of an indication sign.
questions.question: The sign showing that parking is allowed is a regulatory sign.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 2(6) an auxiliary sign states the reason for the restriction and specifies times, days of the week, types of vehicle and so on.
questions.question: The only thing an auxiliary sign can specify is the times during which the restriction applies.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(1) a vehicle or streetcar already turning left may carry on even on a red light for that direction.
questions.question: A streetcar (tram) already turning left at an intersection must stop where it is once the light for that direction turns red.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 3(2) it is given as an example of an indication marking.
questions.question: The marking showing where vehicles stop is a regulatory marking.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under the note to Kyosoku Appendix 1(1) it is just before the pedestrian crossing, bicycle crossing or railway crossing.
questions.question: Outside an intersection, where there is a pedestrian crossing the stopping position is the middle of the crossing.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 2(1) the kinds of sign and what they mean are set out in Kyosoku Appendix 3(1).
questions.question: What a sign means is settled by its shape and colour alone, so there is no need to look at the Kyosoku appendix.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 3 item 1. The judgement of the officer on the spot outranks the light.
questions.question: Where a police officer or traffic warden is controlling traffic by hand signal, their signal prevails even if it differs from the traffic light.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 3 item 2. Instructions are given to suit conditions on the spot, such as an accident or road works.
questions.question: An instruction given by a police officer prevails even if it differs from the regulation shown by road signs or markings.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(3)(a). Lowering the arm by itself does not change the meaning.
questions.question: When a police officer lowers the arm without changing the way they are facing, it means the same as raising the arm horizontally to the side.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(3)(a). The same meaning holds while the arm is moving from horizontal to vertical.
questions.question: When a police officer raises an arm vertically, that has the same meaning as an amber light for traffic running parallel to the front of their body.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(3)(b). For traffic crossing that direction it means a red light.
questions.question: When a police officer waves a light from side to side, that has the same meaning as a green light for traffic moving in the direction the light is waved.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(3)(b). For traffic crossing that direction it means a red light.
questions.question: When a police officer holds a light above their head, that has the same meaning as an amber light for traffic moving in the direction the light was being waved before it was raised.

questions.explanation: This is the note to Kyosoku Appendix 1(3)(a). Elsewhere the stopping position is the same as for a traffic light.
questions.question: Where a police officer gives a hand signal outside an intersection at a place with no pedestrian crossing, bicycle crossing or railway crossing, the stopping position is 1 metre short of the officer.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 3 item 2. Individual instructions are to be followed as well as hand-signal traffic control.
questions.question: When a police officer or traffic warden gives a necessary instruction about how to proceed, you must act on that instruction.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(3)(a) it has the same meaning as an amber light.
questions.question: When a police officer raises an arm vertically, that has the same meaning as a green light for traffic running parallel to the front of their body.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(3)(a) crossing traffic gets the same meaning as a red light.
questions.question: When a police officer raises an arm horizontally to the side, that has the same meaning as a green light for traffic crossing the front of their body.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(3)(a) lowering the arm without turning means the same as raising it horizontally to the side.
questions.question: When a police officer lowers the arm without changing the way they are facing, it signals that traffic control has ended, so you may follow the traffic light.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under the note to Kyosoku Appendix 1(3)(a) it is 1 metre short of the officer.
questions.question: Where a police officer gives a hand signal outside an intersection at a place with no pedestrian crossing or railway crossing, the stopping position is 3 metres short of the officer.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(3)(b), for traffic moving in the direction the light was being waved before it was raised, it means an amber light.
questions.question: When a police officer holds a light above their head, it means a red light for traffic in every direction.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 3 item 1 you must follow the hand signals of traffic wardens as well as police officers.
questions.question: A traffic warden's hand signal is only for guidance, and there is no duty to follow it.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(3)(a) that signal means the same as an amber light, so you must not proceed beyond the stopping position.
questions.question: At an intersection a police officer held an arm vertically towards your direction of travel, but you drove into the intersection although you could have stopped safely.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 3 item 1 lays down obedience to traffic-control hand signals as a rule common to pedestrians and drivers alike.
questions.question: Only vehicles have to obey a police officer's hand signal; pedestrians do not.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 4 item 1(5). What is thrown out can strike another vehicle or a pedestrian.
questions.question: You must not throw cigarette ends, waste paper, empty cans and the like out of a vehicle, or put your body or objects outside it.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 4 item 2. A road is a place where many people and vehicles pass.
questions.question: You must not display goods on the road or leave earth, timber or anything else that obstructs traffic on it.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 4 item 1(5) you must not put your body or objects outside the vehicle.
questions.question: Because the vehicle was stuck in a jam and it was dull, you put your arm out of the window to look at what was going on outside.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 4 item 3 forbids putting up such a neon sign at all, so that traffic lights, road signs and road markings stay easy to see.
questions.question: Putting up a neon sign in a colour resembling a traffic light near a traffic light is acceptable as long as it is only lit at night.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 4 item 1(1). The rule binds people who are not driving as well.
questions.question: You must not obstruct traffic on the road by staggering about drunk, standing around talking, sitting down or lying down.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 4 item 1(6). If you fall, the vehicle behind may run over you.
questions.question: You must not grab hold of a moving vehicle or streetcar (tram) from outside.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 4 item 1(7). Losing sight even for a moment can lead to a serious accident.
questions.question: You must not shine a light towards the road that would dazzle a driver.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 4 item 1(8) you must not sprinkle water when it may freeze.
questions.question: Sprinkling water on the road is not prohibited even when it may freeze.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 4 item 1(3) forbids throwing or firing anything towards the road at all.
questions.question: Throwing or firing something towards the road is acceptable as long as it hits nobody.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 4 item 1(1) you must not obstruct traffic by sitting or lying down.
questions.question: Sitting or lying down on the road is not prohibited, even where it obstructs traffic.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 4 item 1(6) you must not grab hold of a moving vehicle or streetcar (tram) from outside.
questions.question: Holding onto a moving vehicle while riding a bicycle is efficient, since you get along fast with little effort.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 2 Section 2 item 1. A pedestrian walks on the roadway only where there is neither.
questions.question: On a road with a sidewalk or a side strip (路側帯) of sufficient width, a pedestrian must use it, except where road works or the like make it impassable.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 2 Section 2 item 3. It lets you see the vehicles coming towards you.
questions.question: On a road with neither a sidewalk nor a side strip (路側帯) of sufficient width, a pedestrian must walk on the right-hand edge of the road.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 2 Section 2 item 5. A motor-vehicle-only road is treated the same as a national expressway.
questions.question: A pedestrian must not enter a road closed to pedestrians by sign, a national expressway or a motor-vehicle-only road.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 2 Section 3 item 1. Where a footbridge or underpass is nearby, use it if you can.
questions.question: Where there is a pedestrian crossing or a signalled intersection nearby, a pedestrian must cross at that crossing or intersection.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 2 Section 3 item 1. Crossing where there is a guard rail is extremely dangerous too.
questions.question: Where the No crossing for pedestrians sign stands, a pedestrian must not cross.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 2 Section 3 item 2(2). If the light looks like changing, do not push it; wait for the next green.
questions.question: Even after the light turns green, cross only once you have confirmed that vehicles and streetcars (trams) to left and right have stopped.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 2 Section 3 item 2(5) you may cross diagonally at a scramble crossing in accordance with the pedestrian signal.
questions.question: A pedestrian must never cross a road diagonally, in any circumstances.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 2 Section 3 item 3(4) you watch what other vehicles are doing and start only once you have confirmed it is safe.
questions.question: Where there is no signal and a vehicle stops for you, you may start crossing at once.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 2 Section 2 item 5 a motor-vehicle-only road and any road closed to pedestrians by sign are also barred.
questions.question: The only road a pedestrian must not enter is a national expressway.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 2 Section 3 item 2(4) you press the button and wait for the light to turn green.
questions.question: Where there is a push-button pedestrian signal you may cross without pressing the button.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 2 Section 3 item 1 you must cross at the crossing where one is nearby.
questions.question: There was a pedestrian crossing about 50 metres ahead, but as you saw no vehicles nearby you crossed the road where you were.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 2 Section 3 item 3(2) you look carefully both ways, with particular care for vehicles coming from the left.
questions.question: When about to cross where there is no signal, it is enough to check for vehicles coming from the right.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 2(2). Being unable to work the pedals reliably is dangerous.
questions.question: Dress so that you can move freely when driving, and do not drive in wooden clogs, high heels or similar footwear.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 2(4). The ring itself is what pulls your attention away.
questions.question: Before driving it is best to switch a smartphone off or set it to driving mode so that it does not ring.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 2(3). It leaves you unable to steer quickly if you need to.
questions.question: Do not drive with your elbow resting on the window frame.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 4(1) an infant must be put in a child seat suited to their stage of growth, and being held is not an exception.
questions.question: Even when carrying an infant in a car, no child seat is needed as long as a guardian is holding them.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 4(2) you must choose one that can be fixed firmly to the seat and fit it securely per the manual, or it loses its effect.
questions.question: A child seat works as long as it fits the child's build, even if it is not fixed to the seat.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 5(2) you give the signal to move off and then check again before starting.
questions.question: To move off you first check in the mirrors that it is safe all round, and give the signal once the vehicle is already moving.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 5(1) you also check that no child is underneath the vehicle.
questions.question: Before getting into the vehicle you only need to check that nobody is in front of or behind it; underneath it need not be checked.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 5(3) moving off in reverse is dangerous, so you back into the garage beforehand.
questions.question: When you put the car into a garage it is best to drive in nose first, so that you can reverse out when you leave.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 2(4) draws no distinction by size of device; it prohibits gazing at the displayed image while moving, full stop.
questions.question: The ban on gazing at a car navigation screen while moving applies only to devices with a large display.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 3(2) you keep the seat back upright, sit well back, and fasten the lap belt around the pelvis.
questions.question: To wear a seat belt correctly you recline the seat back and fasten the lap belt across the abdomen.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 3(2) you also check that the belt is not twisted.
questions.question: As long as the buckle tongue is fully home, it does not matter if the seat belt is twisted.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 5(1) you must check before getting in that nobody is in front of or behind the vehicle and that no child is underneath it.
questions.question: Because you saw nobody about in the car park, you got in without checking around the vehicle and moved off at once.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 4(1) it is infants in particular who must be put in a child seat suited to their stage of growth.
questions.question: The requirement to use a child seat applies only to primary-school children among those who cannot be fitted properly with a seat belt.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 1(1). The step exists to stop you driving off with the door not properly latched.
questions.question: When closing the door after getting in, pause just short of closed and then push it firmly shut.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 3(1). Wearing one is not only for the moment of a crash.
questions.question: A seat belt not only reduces the harm suffered in an accident but also eases fatigue by keeping you in a correct driving posture.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 3(3). Pregnancy differs from person to person.
questions.question: Whether wearing a seat belt during pregnancy suits your health is something to confirm with a doctor.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 4(1). That is why it is used for a child who cannot be fitted properly with a seat belt.
questions.question: A child seat not only reduces the harm suffered in an accident but also keeps the child from interfering with driving.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 2(3). A correct driving posture is the first step to safe driving.
questions.question: Driving with your elbow on the window frame leaves you unable to steer quickly if you need to.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 3(1) it also eases fatigue by keeping you in a correct driving posture.
questions.question: The only effect of a seat belt is to reduce the harm suffered in an accident.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 1(1) you pause just short of closed and then push it firmly shut.
questions.question: When closing the door after getting in it is best to slam it shut in one movement, to avoid leaving it half latched.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 4(2) you choose one that fits the child's build and can be fixed firmly to the seat, and use it properly.
questions.question: A child seat works as long as it can be fixed to the seat, even if it does not fit the child's build.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 2(3) you are told not to drive with your elbow on the window frame.
questions.question: Driving with an elbow on the window frame is relaxing and therefore suits long trips.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 3(3) wearing it properly during pregnancy protects both mother and baby from harm in an accident.
questions.question: During pregnancy it is safer for mother and baby not to wear a seat belt.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 1. That is the rule of keeping left, and the exceptions are only those set out in the same item.
questions.question: A vehicle must travel on the part of the road to the left of the centre (or of the center line where there is one).

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 1(3). Where the No overtaking on the right-hand side of the road sign or marking is in place, this exception is not available.
questions.question: You may cross onto the right-hand side of the road to overtake on a road with a clear view whose left-hand side is under 6 metres wide, except where a road sign or road marking prohibits crossing over to overtake.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 2(1). Within the left-hand side of the road you keep further to the left still.
questions.question: On a road without vehicle lanes you must keep to the left of the road, except where overtaking or something similar makes it unavoidable.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 2(2). The right-hand lane is left free for overtaking and the like.
questions.question: Where there are two vehicle lanes in the same direction, you must travel in the left-hand lane.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 2(2). In the other lanes, slower vehicles travel further left and faster ones progressively further right.
questions.question: Where there are three or more vehicle lanes in the same direction, the rightmost lane must be left free for overtaking.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 2(3). The rightmost lane exists to be kept free for overtaking.
questions.question: Even after using the rightmost lane to overtake, you must return promptly to one of the other lanes once you have finished overtaking.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 3. As a rule you stay in the same lane.
questions.question: On a road with vehicle lanes you must not stray out of your lane or straddle two lanes, except where overtaking or something similar makes it unavoidable.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 2(2). A specification by sign or marking overrides the general lane rule.
questions.question: Where a road sign or road marking specifies how lanes are to be used, you must follow that specification rather than the general rule about vehicle lanes.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 2(2) the lane you travel in is the left-hand one.
questions.question: Where there are two vehicle lanes in the same direction, you must travel in the right-hand lane.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 2(2) the rightmost lane must be left free for overtaking.
questions.question: On a road with three or more lanes you may stay in the rightmost lane whenever you want to travel fast.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 3 you may straddle lanes only where overtaking or something similar makes it unavoidable, and whether anyone is behind you makes no difference.
questions.question: On a road with vehicle lanes, straddling two lanes is acceptable as long as there is nobody behind you.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 2(2) the rightmost lane is kept free for overtaking, and being in a hurry is not a reason.
questions.question: On a road with three lanes, you stayed in the rightmost lane because you were running late for an appointment.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 2(2) slower vehicles travel further left and faster ones progressively further right.
questions.question: Where there are three or more lanes, faster vehicles travel in the left-hand lanes and slower ones progressively further right.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 1(4) you may cross over only where the Keep right marking is in place.
questions.question: Near a bend on a steeply graded road you may cross onto the right-hand side even where there is no road marking.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 1, except on a one-way road, you must keep the amount you cross over as small as you can.
questions.question: When you cross onto the right-hand side of a road that is not one way, how far you cross over is not in question.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 2(2), where there are two lanes you must travel in the left-hand one.
questions.question: On a road with two vehicle lanes in the same direction you may travel in either lane.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 5. Stopping inside the intersection would block the emergency vehicle's path.
questions.question: When an emergency vehicle approaches, near an intersection you must keep clear of the intersection, pull over to the left of the road and come to a complete stop (一時停止).

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 5. A complete stop is not required there, but you must still give way.
questions.question: When an emergency vehicle approaches, at places other than near an intersection you must pull over to the left of the road and give way.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 5. How you give way is decided by what does not obstruct the emergency vehicle.
questions.question: On a one-way road, where pulling over to the left would get in the emergency vehicle's way instead, you must pull over to the right.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 6(1). The duty to give way is not owed at the cost of creating danger.
questions.question: When a route bus stopped at a stop signals that it is moving off, a vehicle behind must not obstruct it, except where avoiding it would take sudden braking or sudden steering.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 6(2). Those three kinds of vehicle are the ones excluded from the restriction.
questions.question: Even on a road with a lane designated for route buses, small special vehicles, motorized bicycles and light road vehicles may use that lane.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 6(2). The restriction is aimed at travelling along the lane, not at crossing it.
questions.question: Even in a lane designated for route buses you may use it when pulling to the right edge, the centre or the left edge of the road in order to turn, and where road works or the like leave no alternative.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 6(3). Unlike a designated lane, a priority lane may be used by other cars as well.
questions.question: A car travelling in a lane where route buses have priority must leave that lane promptly when a route bus approaches.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 6(3). By the time you cannot get out, you are already obstructing the bus.
questions.question: Where traffic is congested and you might be unable to leave the priority lane once a route bus approaches, you must not enter that lane in the first place.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 6(2). The set of vehicles excluded differs from that for a route bus lane.
questions.question: On a road with a lane designated for ordinary bicycles, every vehicle other than a specified small motorized bicycle or a light road vehicle must stay out of that lane.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 5. Near an intersection you keep clear of it and stop; elsewhere you pull to the left and give way.
questions.question: Whether you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) or need only give way when making room for an emergency vehicle depends on whether you are near an intersection.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 5 you keep clear of the intersection, pull to the left of the road and stop.
questions.question: When an emergency vehicle approaches, near an intersection you must move into the intersection first and then pull to the left and come to a complete stop (一時停止).

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 5 it is enough to pull to the left and give way there; a complete stop is not required.
questions.question: When an emergency vehicle approaches, at places other than near an intersection you must pull to the left of the road and come to a complete stop (一時停止).

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 5, where pulling to the left would get in the emergency vehicle's way instead, you must pull to the right.
questions.question: On a one-way road too, it is enough to pull over to the left of the road and give way when an emergency vehicle approaches.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 6(1) the only exception is where avoiding it would take sudden braking or sudden steering.
questions.question: Even when a route bus at a stop has signalled that it is moving off, you may obstruct it as long as your own vehicle can get past first.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 6(2), small special vehicles, motorized bicycles and light road vehicles are excluded.
questions.question: On a road with a lane designated for route buses, no vehicle at all may use that lane.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 6(2) pulling to the right edge, the centre or the left edge of the road in order to turn is an exception, as are road works and the like.
questions.question: On a road with a lane designated for route buses you must not enter that lane even in order to turn right or left.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 6(3), if congestion might leave you unable to get out, you must not enter the lane in the first place.
questions.question: A car in a lane where route buses have priority need not leave it when a bus approaches, as long as the traffic is congested.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 5 you must keep clear of the intersection, pull to the left of the road and come to a complete stop (一時停止).
questions.question: An emergency vehicle came up behind you just before an intersection, and because the intersection was close you drove into it before pulling left and stopping.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 6(2), specified small motorized bicycles and light road vehicles may use that lane.
questions.question: On a road with a lane designated for ordinary bicycles, every vehicle other than a bicycle must stay out of that lane.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 6(3), if congestion might leave you unable to get out, you must not enter the lane in the first place.
questions.question: You may keep travelling in a lane where route buses have priority even in congestion, as long as no bus is approaching.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(2). Even when crossing, you must come to a complete stop just before it.
questions.question: A vehicle must not travel along a sidewalk, a side strip (路側帯) or a bicycle path, except when crossing one to enter or leave a place facing the road.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(3). Entering is prohibited even if you would only be passing through.
questions.question: You must not enter a safety zone or a place where the No entry zone road marking prohibits vehicles.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(4). The shoulder crumbles easily and is not strong enough to carry a vehicle.
questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk and no side strip (路側帯), you must not stray onto the shoulder, the 0.5 metres measured from the edge of the road.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(5). Crossing the tracks in order to turn right is allowed even without the sign.
questions.question: A vehicle must not travel on tram tracks, except where a vehicle permitted by the Driving on tram tracks permitted sign does so, or where it is turning right and similar cases.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(6). Even a vehicle allowed on the tracks must not obstruct the streetcar.
questions.question: A vehicle travelling on tram tracks must, when a streetcar (tram) comes up behind it, leave the tracks promptly or keep a sufficient distance.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 4. These vehicles are taller than ordinary ones, and the load on the bed can push them over the limit.
questions.question: When taking a large, medium or semi-medium vehicle through a place with a height limit, you must check that it is within the limit including the height of the load.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(1). The same goes for a road carrying the Pedestrians only sign.
questions.question: You must not travel on a road where signs such as Road closed or Closed to all vehicles prohibit it.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(4). Where there is a sidewalk or a side strip, travelling on it is already prohibited in itself.
questions.question: The ban on straying onto the shoulder applies when you are travelling on a road that has no sidewalk and no side strip (路側帯).

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(2). Crossing it to enter or leave a place facing the road is an exception.
questions.question: A bicycle path is a place for bicycles and similar vehicles, and a car must not travel along it.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(3). When you pass a safety zone with people in it you must also proceed slowly (徐行).
questions.question: A safety zone is a place a vehicle must not enter, whether or not anyone is standing in it.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(4) the shoulder is the 0.5 metres from the edge of the road.
questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk and no side strip (路側帯), the shoulder is the 1 metre measured from the edge of the road.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(2), crossing one to enter or leave a place facing the road is an exception.
questions.question: A vehicle must never cross a sidewalk or a side strip (路側帯), in any circumstances.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(5) only vehicles permitted by the Driving on tram tracks permitted sign, and cases such as turning right, are allowed.
questions.question: Any vehicle may travel on tram tracks once it has confirmed that no streetcar (tram) is running nearby.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(6) it must leave the tracks promptly or keep a sufficient distance.
questions.question: A vehicle allowed onto the tram tracks by the Driving on tram tracks permitted sign may carry on as it is even when a streetcar (tram) comes up behind it.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(3) you must not enter a place where that marking prohibits vehicles.
questions.question: Even where the No entry zone road marking is in place, you may pass through it if no vehicle is inside.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 4 the load on the bed can itself exceed the limit, so it is checked as well.
questions.question: What you have to check at a place with a height limit is the height of the vehicle body alone; the load on the bed is not included.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(4) draws no distinction by type of vehicle, and there is no exception for two-wheelers.
questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk and no side strip (路側帯) you must not stray onto the shoulder, but two-wheeled vehicles are excepted.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(1) a road closed by sign may not be used, and living there is not a reason.
questions.question: Even on a road carrying the Closed to all vehicles sign, you may drive along it if your own home is further down it.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(2) a vehicle must not travel along a sidewalk.
questions.question: Because the road was jammed and you could not move on, you drove up onto the empty sidewalk and went forward.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(3) a vehicle must not enter a safety zone. Proceeding slowly is what is required when you pass a safety zone with people in it.
questions.question: A safety zone is a place for pedestrians to wait, so a vehicle may enter it but must proceed slowly (徐行).

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 1(2). Here too you keep the amount you cross over as small as you can.
questions.question: Where road works or the like leave the left-hand side too narrow to pass, you may cross onto the right-hand side of the road.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 1(1). This is the one case in which the limit on how far you cross over does not apply.
questions.question: On a one-way road you may cross onto the right-hand side of the road.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 6(2). The same goes for pulling to the edge or the centre of the road in order to turn.
questions.question: Even on a road with a lane designated for route buses you may use that lane where road works or the like leave no alternative.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(5). The same goes for a vehicle permitted by the Driving on tram tracks permitted sign.
questions.question: Crossing the tram tracks in order to turn right is allowed.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 2(2). The specification takes precedence over the guidance about sorting by speed.
questions.question: Even on a road with three or more lanes, where signs or markings specify how lanes are to be used you travel as specified.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(2). Even when crossing, you must come to a complete stop just before it.
questions.question: Crossing a sidewalk or side strip (路側帯) is allowed in cases such as entering or leaving a place facing the road.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 3. Changing lanes needlessly troubles following vehicles and causes accidents.
questions.question: On a road with vehicle lanes you must not change lanes without good reason; you stay in the same lane.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 5. Elsewhere you pull over to the left of the road and give way.
questions.question: Keeping clear of the intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches applies where you are near an intersection.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 4. The load itself can also exceed the limit.
questions.question: Large, medium and semi-medium vehicles are taller than ordinary ones, so particular care is needed where there is a height limit.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 2(2). Once the overtaking is finished you return promptly to the left-hand lane.
questions.question: Where there are two lanes in the same direction, the right-hand lane is kept free for overtaking and the like.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. The exception in Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 1(2) is limited to cases where road works or the like leave the left-hand side too narrow to pass.
questions.question: If the left-hand side feels narrow you may cross onto the right-hand side even without road works.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 6(2) pulling to the edge or the centre of the road to turn, and road works that leave no alternative, are exceptions.
questions.question: No other car may ever use a lane designated for route buses, in any circumstances.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(5) only vehicles permitted by sign, and cases such as turning right, may use the tracks.
questions.question: You may cross the tram tracks even when not turning right, as long as there is little traffic.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(2) crossing it to enter or leave a place facing the road is an exception.
questions.question: A bicycle path must never be used at all, crossing it included.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 5 you keep clear of the intersection, pull to the left of the road and stop.
questions.question: When an emergency vehicle approaches it is enough to pull left and come to a complete stop (一時停止) inside the intersection.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 3 you must not change lanes without good reason and must stay in the same lane.
questions.question: On a road with vehicle lanes you may change lanes as often as you like so long as you do not straddle two.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 7(4) the shoulder is the 0.5 metres from the edge of the road.
questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk and no side strip (路側帯), the shoulder is the 1.5 metres from the edge of the road.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 4 calls for care in large, medium and semi-medium vehicles alike.
questions.question: Checking the height at a place with a height limit is required only when driving a large vehicle.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 1, except on a one-way road you must keep the amount you cross over as small as you can.
questions.question: The limit on how far you cross over does not apply on roads other than one-way ones either.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 4 you must check that the height including the load on the bed is within the limit.
questions.question: You were carrying a tall load on the bed, but as the body itself was within the limit you drove through a place with a height restriction.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 7(2). These vehicles are unstable and structurally have nothing to protect the rider's body.
questions.question: When you pass a specified small motorized bicycle or a bicycle, for overtaking or any other reason, you must anticipate that it may wobble and either leave a safe clearance or proceed slowly (徐行).

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 1(1). Where a safe clearance cannot be left, you proceed slowly instead.
questions.question: When you pass a pedestrian you must either leave a safe clearance between your vehicle and the pedestrian or proceed slowly (徐行).

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 1(3). Those two cases are the only ones in which you may proceed slowly.
questions.question: Behind a streetcar (tram) stopped at a stop you must stop and wait until nobody is getting on or off, but you may proceed slowly (徐行) when nobody is getting on or off and there is at least 1.5 metres between you and the streetcar, or when there is a safety zone.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 3. The same applies to a person travelling in a vehicle for people with disabilities.
questions.question: When a person carrying a white or yellow cane or accompanied by a guide dog is walking, you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) or proceed slowly (徐行) so that they can pass safely.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 6(2). The stop is required even when there is no pedestrian there.
questions.question: When you cross a sidewalk or a side strip (路側帯) to enter or leave a place facing the road, you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) just before it and must not obstruct pedestrians.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 4(2). A child may run out from in front of or behind the bus.
questions.question: When you pass a stopped school or kindergarten bus, you must proceed slowly (徐行) and check that it is safe.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 1(3) you may proceed slowly (徐行) when nobody is getting on or off and there is at least 1.5 metres between you and the streetcar, or when there is a safety zone.
questions.question: Behind a streetcar (tram) stopped at a stop you must always stop and wait until nobody is getting on or off.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 2(4) prohibits both overtaking and passing without changing lanes in that place.
questions.question: Within a pedestrian crossing and the 30 metres before it, only overtaking is prohibited; passing a vehicle at its side without changing course is not.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 6(1) only vehicles specially permitted may use a pedestrian-only road, and even then they must proceed slowly (徐行) with care for pedestrians.
questions.question: A vehicle with a garage on a pedestrian-only road may use that road even without being specially permitted to.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 4(2) you must proceed slowly (徐行) and check that it is safe when passing a stopped school bus, whatever the view is like.
questions.question: Because the road had a clear view, you passed a stopped school or kindergarten bus at 40 km/h without slowing.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 8(1). The same goes for cars displaying the older driver's, hearing-impaired or disabled-driver marks and for cars being driven on a provisional licence.
questions.question: Except where it is unavoidable to avoid danger, you must not squeeze in alongside an ordinary car displaying the beginner's mark or force your way in front of it.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 8(2). It is laid down alongside the ban on squeezing in and cutting in.
questions.question: The driver of a car displaying the hearing-impaired mark may not hear the horn, so show consideration so that they can travel safely.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 1(4). Splashing a pedestrian is exactly the nuisance the rule is about.
questions.question: Where there is mud or a puddle you must proceed slowly (徐行) or otherwise take care not to splash mud or water over anyone.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 1(5). A stopped vehicle is also an obstacle that blocks your view.
questions.question: When you pass a stopped vehicle, take care: a door may suddenly open, or someone may dart out from behind it.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 2(1). A pedestrian in the act of crossing is protected whether or not there is a crossing.
questions.question: Where a pedestrian is crossing at or near an intersection that has no pedestrian crossing, you must not obstruct them.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 2(5). Crossing away from a pedestrian crossing is not always an offence.
questions.question: Even where there is no pedestrian or bicycle crossing, pedestrians may cross, so take care.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 9. Doing it as a group makes the danger greater.
questions.question: When driving in a group you must not do things that endanger or inconvenience other vehicles, such as zigzagging or hemming them in.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 10. Particular care is needed at night and in residential areas.
questions.question: You must not make the kind of noise that seriously disturbs others by pulling away sharply, accelerating hard or revving the engine.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 8(1)(f). It is listed as a protected case, not by the mark it carries.
questions.question: A car being driven by someone practising on a provisional licence is among those you must not squeeze in alongside or force your way in front of.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 1(1). You choose between clearance and slowing; doing neither is not an option.
questions.question: Where you cannot leave a safe clearance when passing a pedestrian, you must proceed slowly (徐行).

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 8(1) squeezing in and forcing your way in are prohibited except where unavoidable to avoid danger.
questions.question: A car with the beginner's mark is driven awkwardly, so you may squeeze past it to get ahead sooner.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 8(1) cars with the older driver's, hearing-impaired or disabled-driver marks and cars driven on a provisional licence are covered too.
questions.question: Squeezing in and forcing your way in front are prohibited only in relation to cars displaying the beginner's mark.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 1(4) you must proceed slowly (徐行) or otherwise take care not to splash anyone.
questions.question: Even where there is a puddle you may go through without slowing, as long as there is some distance to the pedestrian.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 2(1) you must not obstruct a pedestrian crossing at or near an intersection that has no crossing.
questions.question: At an intersection with no pedestrian crossing it does not matter if you obstruct a pedestrian who is crossing.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 10 you must not rev the engine in a way that makes noise seriously disturbing to others.
questions.question: Revving the engine does the car no harm, so it is not a problem even in a residential area.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 2(5) pedestrians may cross even where there is no pedestrian or bicycle crossing, so take care.
questions.question: Pedestrians never cross where there is no pedestrian crossing, so there is no need to watch for them at such places.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 8(2) such a driver may not hear the horn, so you show consideration so that they can travel safely.
questions.question: It is best to sound the horn to let the driver of a car with the hearing-impaired mark know you are there.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 1(5) you also watch for a door opening suddenly and for someone darting out from behind it.
questions.question: The only thing to watch for when passing a stopped vehicle is that it may suddenly move off.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 9 you must not zigzag or otherwise endanger or inconvenience other vehicles.
questions.question: When driving in a group a little zigzagging is acceptable to keep the formation together.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 1(4) you must proceed slowly (徐行) or otherwise take care not to splash anyone.
questions.question: There was a pedestrian on the sidewalk of a road with a puddle, but you were running late, so you went through at the same speed and splashed them.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 4(1). A child absorbed in something interesting may suddenly run out into the road.
questions.question: Where a child is walking alone you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) or proceed slowly (徐行) so that they can pass safely.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 4(3). You reduce speed even when no child is in sight.
questions.question: Near a school, kindergarten or amusement park, and where the school-route sign stands, children may dart out suddenly, so take particular care.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 5. Older people walk more slowly and tend to be slower to notice and avoid danger.
questions.question: Where an older person who has difficulty getting about is passing, such as one walking with a stick or using a walking aid, you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) or proceed slowly (徐行) so that they can pass safely.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 5. Watch out for what a stopped vehicle hides as well.
questions.question: Accidents involving older pedestrians happen most often when they cross just in front of or just behind a vehicle.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 7(1). They are unstable and structurally have nothing to protect the rider's body.
questions.question: A specified small motorized bicycle or a bicycle is a kind of vehicle and travels on the roadway as a rule.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 7(3). It matches the duty to stop for pedestrians.
questions.question: When you cross a sidewalk, side strip (路側帯) or bicycle path to enter or leave a place facing the road, you come to a complete stop (一時停止) just before it and check for specified small motorized bicycles and bicycles.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 7(4). Drive on the assumption that the rider has not noticed you.
questions.question: When going through an intersection, take care not to draw in a specified small motorized bicycle or bicycle travelling on your left, and check as you go whether its rider is aware of your car.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 6(1). Permission does not change the fact that the road belongs to pedestrians.
questions.question: When a vehicle specially permitted to use a pedestrian-only road does so, it must proceed slowly (徐行) with care for pedestrians.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 3. The same goes for a person with a white or yellow cane or with a guide dog.
questions.question: Where someone is travelling in a vehicle for people with disabilities, you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) or proceed slowly (徐行) so that they can pass safely.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 4(1). Do not expect a child to judge as an adult would.
questions.question: Part of why a child walking alone needs care is that their judgement is immature, so they may try to cross the road when they should not.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 3 you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) or proceed slowly (徐行) when such a person is walking.
questions.question: Even where a person with a white or yellow cane is present, you need neither stop nor slow down as long as they are not about to cross.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 5 deals with an older person with difficulty getting about who is passing, and sets no limit as to place.
questions.question: Stopping or slowing for an older person walking is required only when they are using a pedestrian crossing.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 items 7(3) and 6(2) you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) just before crossing a sidewalk.
questions.question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter a car park you need not stop if there is no pedestrian.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 4(2) you must proceed slowly (徐行) and check that it is safe.
questions.question: When passing a stopped school or kindergarten bus you need not slow down if no child is getting off.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 6(1) it must proceed slowly with particular care for pedestrians.
questions.question: On a pedestrian-only road a permitted vehicle need not proceed slowly (徐行) as long as it watches for pedestrians.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 7(1) they are a kind of vehicle and travel on the roadway as a rule.
questions.question: A specified small motorized bicycle or a bicycle is close to a pedestrian, so it travels on the sidewalk as a rule.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 4(3) children may dart out suddenly at such places, so particular care is required.
questions.question: Where the school-route sign stands you need take care only when a child is in sight.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 7(4) you check as you go whether the rider is aware of your car.
questions.question: Watching for bicycles at an intersection proceeds on the basis that the rider has noticed your car.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 5 older people generally walk more slowly and less steadily.
questions.question: Older people generally walk faster, so you may allow less time for them to cross.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 4(1) you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) or proceed slowly (徐行) where a child is walking alone.
questions.question: A child was walking alone at the roadside but showed no sign of crossing, so you went past at the same speed.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 2(1). A vehicle cannot stop instantly, so you drive at a speed from which this stopping distance still lets you stop safely.
questions.question: Stopping distance is the reaction distance the vehicle travels between the driver sensing danger and the brakes actually beginning to work, plus the braking distance from the moment the brakes begin to work until the vehicle stops.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 2(2). Reaction distance changes with the condition of the driver.
questions.question: When the driver is tired it takes longer to recognise danger and decide what to do, so the reaction distance becomes longer.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 4. The test is not a particular figure but whether you can stop at once.
questions.question: To proceed slowly (徐行) means to move at a speed from which the vehicle can stop immediately.
