questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 4(4). A downhill stretch that is not steep is not one of these places.
questions.question: You must proceed slowly (徐行) when travelling near the crest of a hill or on a steep downgrade.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 2(4). Because you look down from the driving seat, what you feel and the real distance drift apart.
questions.question: Large, medium and semi-medium vehicles have a higher driving position than ordinary vehicles, so the following distance feels longer than it really is and tends to become too short.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 3(2). This way of braking is particularly effective when the road is slippery.
questions.question: Using the brakes in several separate applications makes the brake lights flash, which signals to the vehicle behind and helps prevent a rear-end collision.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 3(3). In this case you do not use the several-separate-applications method.
questions.question: When braking hard in a vehicle fitted with an anti-lock braking system (ABS), you have to press the brake pedal hard in one go and keep it pressed so that the system works.

questions.explanation: This is Article 11 of the Road Traffic Act Enforcement Order as it stands from 1 September 2026. On an ordinary road that has a center line or vehicle lanes, or that is divided by a median strip, it remains 60 km/h.
questions.question: On an ordinary road that has no center line and no vehicle lanes and is not divided by direction with a median strip, and where no maximum speed is posted by road sign or road marking, the legal maximum speed for a car is 30 km/h.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 1(1) forbids driving above the maximum speed shown by a sign or marking, and there is no exception for keeping up with the flow.
questions.question: Even on a road where a maximum speed is posted by road sign or road marking, you may exceed it in order to keep up with the flow of surrounding traffic.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 4(2) excepts intersections under traffic control by a traffic light and cases where you are travelling on a priority road.
questions.question: You must proceed slowly (徐行) whenever you go through an intersection with poor visibility to left and right, without exception.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 3(3) you press hard in one go and keep the pedal pressed so that the system works.
questions.question: When braking hard in a vehicle fitted with an anti-lock braking system (ABS), you must press the brake pedal in several separate applications.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 2(4) requires you to take the weather, the state of the road and tyres and the weight of the load into account when keeping your distance.
questions.question: A following distance only has to be one at which you would not run into the vehicle ahead if it stopped suddenly, so the weather, the road surface and the weight of the load need not be taken into account.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 1(2) a general motorized bicycle must not be ridden above 30 km/h, and a higher posted speed does not change that.
questions.question: On a road where a sign posts a maximum speed of 40 km/h, a general motorized bicycle (moped) may be ridden at up to 40 km/h.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 1(3) asks you to drive at a safe speed with the road and traffic conditions, the weather and the visibility in mind, even within the permitted speed.
questions.question: As long as you stay within the posted maximum speed, you do not need to slow down even when rain makes visibility poor.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 3(3) allows it only where it is unavoidable to avoid danger, and an empty road behind is not such a reason.
questions.question: Sudden braking is not allowed except where it is unavoidable in order to avoid danger, but it is allowed when there is no vehicle behind you.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 3(1) asks you to press as lightly as you can at first and then build up gradually to the strength you need.
questions.question: If you have already decided where you want to stop, you may press the brake straight to the strength you need from the start.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 4(1). Three other places are laid down besides this sign.
questions.question: You must proceed slowly (徐行) when passing a place carrying the Proceed slowly sign.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 4(2). Those two are the only exceptions.
questions.question: You must proceed slowly (徐行) through an intersection with poor visibility to left and right, except where traffic is controlled by a light and where you are travelling on a priority road.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 4(3). A bend is also a place where overtaking is prohibited.
questions.question: You must proceed slowly (徐行) when passing near a bend in the road.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 1(2). Passing an empty safety zone does not call for slowing.
questions.question: You must proceed slowly (徐行) when you pass a safety zone with people in it.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 1(3). The maximum speed is a ceiling, not a speed you may always travel at.
questions.question: Even within the permitted speed you must drive at a safe speed, with the road and traffic conditions, the weather and the visibility in mind.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 4. The speed from which you can stop at once changes with the road surface and the load.
questions.question: Proceeding slowly (徐行) means moving at a speed from which the vehicle can stop at once; it is not fixed as a figure.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 3(1). You must also refrain from obstructing vehicles on the crossing road.
questions.question: At an intersection without traffic control you must proceed slowly (徐行) where the crossing road is clearly wider.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 3(3). Slowing is required just as it is for a turn at an intersection.
questions.question: To turn in order to leave the road you must first move to the edge or the centre of the road and then proceed slowly (徐行).

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 1(2). Where the posted speed is higher than 30 km/h, 30 km/h is the ceiling.
questions.question: Where a sign posts a maximum speed of 30 km/h or less, a general motorized bicycle (moped) must not be ridden above that posted speed.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 4(4). Near the crest of a hill is one of the same places.
questions.question: You must proceed slowly (徐行) on a steep downgrade.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 4(2). The same holds where traffic is controlled by a light.
questions.question: Even at an intersection with poor visibility to left and right, you need not proceed slowly (徐行) while travelling on a priority road.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 4, proceeding slowly means moving at a speed from which the vehicle can stop at once.
questions.question: Where the Proceed slowly sign stands you need not slow to a speed from which you could stop at once; being slower than those around you is enough.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. The places Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 4(4) names are near the crest of a hill and a steep downgrade.
questions.question: You must proceed slowly (徐行) even on a downhill stretch that is not steep.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 4(2) control by a traffic light is an exception.
questions.question: At an intersection with poor visibility to left and right you must proceed slowly (徐行) even where traffic is controlled by a light.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 1(2) requires slowing when you pass a safety zone with people in it.
questions.question: You must proceed slowly (徐行) when passing a safety zone even if nobody is in it.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 1(2) a general motorized bicycle must not be ridden above 30 km/h.
questions.question: Where a sign posts a maximum speed of 50 km/h, a general motorized bicycle (moped) may be ridden up to that speed.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 4(3) names the area near a bend in the road as the place to slow.
questions.question: What must be taken slowly (徐行) is the bend itself; the area near it is not included.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 4(3) you must proceed slowly (徐行) near a bend whatever the view.
questions.question: Because the bend had a clear view, you turned the wheel and went through without slowing.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 2(1). That is the reaction distance.
questions.question: Before a vehicle stops it covers the distance it travels between the driver sensing danger, pressing the brake, and the brakes actually beginning to work.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 2(4). The distance is not fixed; it changes with the conditions.
questions.question: You must keep a following distance at which you would not run into the vehicle ahead if it stopped suddenly, taking the weather, the state of the road and tyres and the weight of the load into account.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 3(2). The flashing brake lights also signal to the vehicle behind.
questions.question: Braking in several separate applications is particularly effective when the road is slippery.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 3(4). A sudden loss of speed is dangerous for the vehicle behind too.
questions.question: Do not use the brakes needlessly; slow down gradually with the accelerator as far as you can before stopping.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 2(2). What changes the reaction distance is the driver's condition.
questions.question: Braking distance grows longer on a road wet with rain and when a heavy load is carried.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 2(4). That is why the distance tends to become too short, and why care is needed.
questions.question: In a large or medium vehicle you look down from the driving seat, so the following distance feels longer than it is.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 3(1). Pressing hard straight away upsets the vehicle's balance.
questions.question: Press the brake as lightly as you can at first and then build up gradually to the strength you need.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 2(1). It starts from the premise that a vehicle cannot stop instantly.
questions.question: Drive at a speed from which you could still stop safely if danger arose, bearing the stopping distance in mind.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 3(3). For a vehicle with an anti-lock braking system (ABS), how to press the pedal then is laid down.
questions.question: Hard braking is allowed only where it is unavoidable in order to avoid danger.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 2(2) what grows longer on a wet road is the braking distance. Reaction distance grows when the driver is tired and in similar cases.
questions.question: Reaction distance grows longer when driving on a road wet with rain.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 2(4) you set the following distance with the weather, the state of the road and tyres and the weight of the load in mind.
questions.question: As long as you keep a constant distance from the vehicle ahead, you need not change it when the weather changes.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 3(2) the method is particularly effective when the road is slippery.
questions.question: Braking in several separate applications is effective only when the road is dry.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 2(3) it can stretch to about twice as long.
questions.question: With a wet road and worn tyres the stopping distance shrinks to about half of what it is on a dry road with good tyres.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 3(1) you press as lightly as you can at first and then build up gradually.
questions.question: It is better to press the brake straight to the strength you need from the start, because it shortens the stopping distance.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 2(4), looking down from the driving seat makes it feel longer than it is.
questions.question: In a large vehicle the high driving position makes the following distance feel shorter than it is.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 3(4) you avoid needless braking and slow down gradually with the accelerator as far as you can.
questions.question: When reducing speed it is best to manage it with the brakes alone as far as possible.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 2(1) that is the braking distance; stopping distance is the reaction distance plus the braking distance.
questions.question: Stopping distance is the distance from the brakes beginning to work until the vehicle stops.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 3(3) hard braking is allowed only where it is unavoidable to avoid danger.
questions.question: You may brake hard freely as long as you have confirmed that no vehicle is behind you.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 2(2) a tired driver takes longer to recognise and decide, so the reaction distance grows longer.
questions.question: Even when the driver is tired, the time taken to recognise danger and decide does not change.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 2(4) you must set the following distance with the weather and the state of the road in mind.
questions.question: It began to rain, but you carried on with the same following distance as always.

questions.explanation: This is Article 53 paragraph 2 of the Road Traffic Act. At a roundabout a signal is required when leaving and when performing these actions.
questions.question: You must signal when you are about to proceed slowly (徐行), stop or reverse inside a roundabout.

questions.explanation: This is Article 53 paragraphs 2 and 4 of the Road Traffic Act. You must also not signal when you are not going to perform the action.
questions.question: A signal given at a roundabout must be kept up until the action is finished, and stopped promptly once it is.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. If you are taking the exit immediately after entering the roundabout, you signal at the moment you enter it.
questions.question: The signal for leaving a roundabout is given when you have passed the side of the exit immediately before the one you intend to take, whichever exit that is.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(2) has you check that it is safe in the rear-view mirror and so on first, and signal after that.
questions.question: When you are about to leave a roundabout you signal first and then check behind you in the rear-view mirror and so on.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(1). The same 30 metres applies to a right turn or a U-turn.
questions.question: The signal for a left turn is given on reaching the point 30 metres before where you intend to turn, or before the intersection if you are turning there.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(1). The timing is worked out differently from the 30 metres before a turn.
questions.question: The signal for changing course to the left or right while continuing in the same direction is given about three seconds before you change.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(1). The timing is when you are about to slow or stop.
questions.question: The signal for slowing or stopping is given by the brake lights, or by putting an arm out of the vehicle and extending it diagonally downwards.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(1). The moving arm is what distinguishes it from the hand signal for slowing or stopping.
questions.question: The signal for reversing is given by the reversing lights, or by putting an arm out, extending it diagonally downwards with the palm facing back and moving it to and fro.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(3). An unnecessary signal misleads other drivers.
questions.question: A signal must be stopped promptly once the action is finished, and you must not signal when there is no need to.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(4). A hand signal can either replace the indicator or be used alongside it.
questions.question: Where the turn indicator is hard to see because of reflected evening sun or the like, give a hand signal as well as operating the indicator.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(5). Within a Sound horn zone the places where you sound it are limited.
questions.question: You must sound the horn when passing a place carrying the Sound horn sign.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(5). You do not sound it everywhere inside the zone.
questions.question: Within a Sound horn zone you must sound the horn when passing an intersection, a bend or the crest of a hill where the view is blocked.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(5). Sounding it to greet someone or to hurry them along is not allowed.
questions.question: You may sound the horn where it is unavoidable in order to avoid danger, but you must not sound it outside the cases laid down.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(1). The hand signal for a right turn or U-turn is exactly the other way round.
questions.question: The hand signal for a left turn is made by putting the right arm out of the right side of the vehicle and bending it vertically up at the elbow, or by putting the left arm out of the left side and extending it horizontally.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(1) it is given on reaching the point 30 metres before.
questions.question: The signal for a left turn is given on reaching the point 10 metres before where you intend to turn.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(1) a course-change signal is given about three seconds before you change.
questions.question: The signal for changing course while continuing in the same direction is given 30 metres before the point where you change.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(5) the horn may be sounded only at places carrying the sign and where it is unavoidable to avoid danger.
questions.question: When the car ahead is dawdling and getting in your way, you may sound the horn to prompt the driver.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(5) you must sound it when passing an intersection, a bend or the crest of a hill where the view is blocked.
questions.question: Within a Sound horn zone you must sound the horn wherever you pass inside that zone.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 items 1(1) and 1(3) the timing is fixed, and you must not signal when there is no need to.
questions.question: Signalling early is safer, so when you plan to turn it is best to signal a good distance in advance.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(1) the arm is extended diagonally downwards.
questions.question: The hand signal for slowing or stopping is made by putting an arm out of the vehicle and extending it horizontally.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(4) you give the hand signal as well as operating the indicator.
questions.question: When reflected evening sun makes the indicator hard to see, you may give only a hand signal and leave the indicator alone.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(1) the left arm is extended horizontally for a left turn. It is the right arm that is bent up at the elbow.
questions.question: The hand signal for a left turn is made by putting the left arm out of the left side and bending it vertically up at the elbow.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(3) you must not signal when there is no need to.
questions.question: It is enough to stop signalling once the action is finished; signalling when you are not going to act is not itself prohibited.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(5) the horn must not be sounded outside places carrying the sign and cases where it is unavoidable to avoid danger.
questions.question: The car ahead stayed stopped without noticing the green light, so you sounded the horn to get it moving.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 2(1). Nor may you change course without good reason.
questions.question: You must not change course where doing so would force a vehicle coming up behind to brake sharply or swerve.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 2(1). The mirrors leave blind areas, so a direct look is needed too.
questions.question: When you have no choice but to change course, do so only after checking that it is safe in the mirrors and with your own eyes.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 2(2). The same applies where a white line has a yellow line running alongside it on your side.
questions.question: Where vehicle lanes are divided by a yellow line, you must not cross that line to change course.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 3(1). The same goes for turning or crossing to enter or leave a place facing the road.
questions.question: You must not cross the road, make a U-turn or reverse where doing so might obstruct pedestrians or the normal progress of other vehicles.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 3(3). You position the vehicle the same way as for a turn at an intersection.
questions.question: To leave the road by turning left you must first keep as far to the left of the road as you can, and to turn right as close to the centre as you can, or to the right edge on a one-way road, and proceed slowly (徐行).

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 3(4). The duty to give way is not owed at the cost of creating danger.
questions.question: Where the vehicle ahead is signalling that it is moving to the left, the centre or the right edge in order to leave the road, you must not obstruct that change of course, except where avoiding it would take sudden braking or sudden steering.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 3(2). That holds even when there is no risk of obstructing other traffic.
questions.question: Where the No crossing for vehicles or No U-turn sign or marking prohibits crossing or turning, you must not cross or make a U-turn.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 2(2). You judge by the colour of the line on your own side.
questions.question: Even where the lanes are divided by a white line, if a yellow line runs alongside it on the side of the lane you are in, you must not cross it to change course.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 2(1). You change course when there is a need to, after checking that it is safe.
questions.question: You must not change course without good reason.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 3(1). It is treated the same as crossing, U-turning and reversing.
questions.question: Turning or crossing in order to enter or leave a place facing the road is likewise forbidden where it might obstruct pedestrians or the normal progress of other vehicles.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 2(2) you must not cross the yellow line to change course, and whether anyone is behind you makes no difference.
questions.question: Even where the lanes are divided by a yellow line, you may cross it to change course if there is nobody behind you.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 2(1) you must not change course where a following vehicle would have to brake sharply or swerve.
questions.question: As long as you have signalled, it does not matter if a vehicle coming up behind has to brake sharply to avoid you.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 3(3) you keep to the centre of the road, or to the right edge on a one-way road, to turn right.
questions.question: To leave the road by turning right you must first keep as far to the left of the road as you can and proceed slowly (徐行).

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 3(2) you must not make a U-turn where a sign or marking prohibits it.
questions.question: Even where the No U-turn sign stands, you may make a U-turn if there is no risk of obstructing other traffic.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 3(4) the case where avoiding it would take sudden braking or sudden steering is an exception.
questions.question: Where the vehicle ahead is signalling that it is moving to the edge of the road in order to leave it, you must never obstruct that change of course, in any circumstances.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 2(1) you check that it is safe in the mirrors and with your own eyes before changing course.
questions.question: Before changing course you need only check the mirrors; a direct look is not required.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 3(1) you must not reverse where it might obstruct pedestrians either.
questions.question: Reversing is prohibited only where it might obstruct the normal progress of other vehicles; pedestrians need not be taken into account.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 2(2) you judge by the colour of the line running alongside the lane you are in.
questions.question: The restriction that the colour of the lane line imposes is judged by the colour of the line on the other side, not your own.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 3(3) you must proceed slowly as well as moving over as far as you can.
questions.question: To leave the road by turning, it is enough to move to the edge or the centre of the road beforehand; proceeding slowly (徐行) is not required.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 2(1) you change course only after checking that it is safe in the mirrors and with your own eyes.
questions.question: Because the lane on the left was clear, you changed into it in one movement after checking only the mirrors.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(1). It is the same 30 metres as for a left turn.
questions.question: The signal for a right turn or a U-turn is given on reaching the point 30 metres before the place, or before the intersection where you turn there.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(1). It is exactly the reverse of the hand signal for a left turn.
questions.question: The hand signal for a right turn or U-turn is made by putting the right arm out of the right side and extending it horizontally, or by putting the left arm out of the left side and bending it vertically up at the elbow.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 2(1). Having signalled is not a ground for the judgement.
questions.question: Whether to change course is judged by whether a vehicle coming up behind would have to brake sharply or swerve.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 3(4). On a one-way road a vehicle may leave the road from the right edge.
questions.question: When the vehicle ahead signals that it is moving to the right edge in order to leave the road, you must not obstruct that change of course either.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(1) it is given on reaching the point 30 metres before.
questions.question: The signal for a right turn is given on reaching the point 10 metres before where you intend to turn.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(1) the right arm is extended horizontally for a right turn. Bending it up at the elbow is the left-turn signal.
questions.question: The hand signal for a right turn is made by putting the right arm out of the right side and bending it vertically up at the elbow.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 2(1) you must not change course where a following vehicle would have to brake sharply or swerve.
questions.question: As long as you have signalled, you need not mind what vehicles coming up behind are doing when changing course.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 3(4) you must not obstruct it whether it moves to the left edge, the centre or the right edge.
questions.question: The only case in which you must not obstruct a vehicle signalling that it is leaving the road is when it moves to the left edge.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(1). Going past the vehicle ahead without changing course is called passing.
questions.question: Overtaking means changing course and coming out in front of a vehicle that is moving ahead of you.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(2)(a). This is called double overtaking.
questions.question: You must not overtake while the vehicle ahead of you is itself overtaking a car.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(2)(c). The same goes for when you would obstruct oncoming vehicles or streetcars (trams).
questions.question: You must not overtake by moving onto the right-hand side of the road if you could only get back to the left-hand side by obstructing the vehicle you passed.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(3)(b). Passing without changing course is prohibited as well as overtaking.
questions.question: Near a bend in the road you must not change course to overtake a car or a general motorized bicycle (moped), nor go past it at its side.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(3)(d). In a tunnel with lanes you may overtake within the lanes.
questions.question: In a tunnel you must not change course to overtake or go past at the side, except where there are vehicle lanes.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(3)(e). Whether you are on a priority road changes the position.
questions.question: At an intersection and within the 30 metres before it you must not change course to overtake or go past at the side, except where you are travelling on a priority road.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(3)(f). There is no exception here of the kind that applies at intersections.
questions.question: At a railway crossing, a pedestrian crossing or a bicycle crossing, and within the 30 metres before it, you must not change course to overtake or go past at the side.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(3)(c). A downhill stretch that is not steep is not one of these places.
questions.question: Near the crest of a hill or on a steep downgrade you must not change course to overtake or go past at the side.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(3)(e) travelling on a priority road is an exception.
questions.question: At an intersection and within the 30 metres before it you must never overtake, in any circumstances.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(3)(d) a tunnel with vehicle lanes is an exception.
questions.question: Inside a tunnel you must never overtake, in any circumstances.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(3) both changing course and going past at the side are prohibited in these places.
questions.question: What is prohibited in a no-overtaking place is overtaking alone; going past at the side without changing course is not.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(2)(d) you must not overtake while the vehicle behind is overtaking you.
questions.question: Even while the vehicle behind is overtaking you, you may overtake the one ahead first.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(1) overtaking involves changing course to come out in front.
questions.question: Overtaking means coming out in front of a moving vehicle ahead without changing course.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(3)(c) a steep downgrade is a no-overtaking place whatever the view.
questions.question: Even on a steep downgrade you may overtake if the view ahead is clear.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(2)(b) you must not overtake while the vehicle ahead is moving to the right.
questions.question: The vehicle ahead had its right indicator on, but because you were faster you overtook it on its right.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(3) overtaking either a car or a general motorized bicycle is prohibited there.
questions.question: In a no-overtaking place only cars may not be overtaken; overtaking a general motorized bicycle (moped) is not prohibited.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 2(1). You pass on the left when the vehicle ahead has moved to the centre to turn right, and when overtaking a streetcar (tram).
questions.question: When you overtake another vehicle you must pass on its right.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 2(1). You also pass on the left when overtaking a streetcar (tram).
questions.question: Where another vehicle has moved to the centre of the road, or to the right edge on a one-way road, in order to turn right, you must overtake it on its left.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 2(2). Where such a clearance is not possible, you hold off overtaking at all.
questions.question: While overtaking you must keep a safe clearance between yourself and the vehicle you are passing.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 2(4). Where there is not enough room for the overtaking, you move as far left as you can and give way.
questions.question: When you are being overtaken you must not increase speed until the overtaking is finished.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 2(3). Staying there leads to speeding and to following too close.
questions.question: Where you have used the rightmost lane to overtake on a road with vehicle lanes, you must return promptly to one of the other lanes once the overtaking is finished.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 3. If you will cross onto the right-hand side of the road, you check that the oncoming side is clear as well.
questions.question: To overtake you first confirm that the place is not a no-overtaking one, then check that it is safe ahead and to the right and right rear, and only then use the right indicator.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 3. The acceleration stays within the maximum speed throughout.
questions.question: In overtaking you move gently to the right about three seconds after using the right indicator, accelerating within the speed limit.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 3. You stop signalling once you are back in your lane.
questions.question: After passing you use the left indicator, carry on until the vehicle you passed can be seen in the rear-view mirror, and then move gently back to the left.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 4. In other situations too you must not cut suddenly in front of another vehicle.
questions.question: When the vehicle ahead has stopped or is moving slowly at an intersection, a railway crossing or the like, you must not cut in front of it or cross in front of it.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 5(2). As a rule it is the vehicle on the obstructed side that waits.
questions.question: Where there is an obstruction ahead in your path, you come to a complete stop (一時停止) or slow down beforehand and give way to oncoming vehicles.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 2(1) you pass a streetcar on its left.
questions.question: To overtake a streetcar (tram) you must pass on its right.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 2(4) you must not increase speed until the overtaking is finished.
questions.question: When you are being overtaken it is best to speed up as well, so the other vehicle can finish sooner.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 3 you use the right indicator and move gently right about three seconds later.
questions.question: In overtaking you move to the right first and use the right indicator after that.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 3 the acceleration must stay within the maximum speed.
questions.question: Since overtaking means going faster than the vehicle ahead, you may accelerate past the maximum speed.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 3 you also check the right side and right rear in the mirrors.
questions.question: Before overtaking you need only check that it is safe ahead; the right rear need not be checked.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 4 you must not cut in front of a vehicle that has stopped or is moving slowly.
questions.question: Even where the vehicle ahead has stopped at an intersection, you may cut in front of it as long as it has not started moving.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 4 you must not cut suddenly in front of another vehicle in other situations either.
questions.question: Cutting in is prohibited only in front of vehicles stopped at an intersection or railway crossing; elsewhere cutting in suddenly is acceptable.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 5(2) it is the vehicle on the obstructed side that stops or slows beforehand and gives way.
questions.question: Where there is an obstruction ahead in your path, it is the oncoming vehicle that must stop or slow down and give way.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 2(3) you must return promptly to one of the other lanes once the overtaking is finished.
questions.question: After overtaking in the rightmost lane you may stay in it, ready for the next overtaking.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 2(2) you must keep a safe clearance from the vehicle you are passing.
questions.question: The road was narrow and you could not leave enough clearance, but you overtook anyway because the other vehicle was a bicycle.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 2(4). You must also not increase speed until the overtaking is finished.
questions.question: When you are being overtaken and there is not enough room for it, you must move as far left as you can and give way.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 3(2). It comes on top of checking ahead and to the right rear.
questions.question: When you will overtake by crossing onto the right-hand side of the road, you do so only after checking that the oncoming side is clear.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 4. Cutting in front of a vehicle stopped at an intersection or railway crossing is prohibited too.
questions.question: You must not cut suddenly in front of another vehicle or squeeze in alongside one travelling beside you.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 5(1). Where there is an obstruction ahead you stop or slow down beforehand and give way.
questions.question: When passing an oncoming vehicle, keep a safe clearance.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(2)(c). The same goes for when you could only return to the left-hand side by obstructing the vehicle you passed.
questions.question: You must not overtake by moving onto the right-hand side of the road where doing so would obstruct oncoming vehicles or streetcars (trams).

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 2(1). In every other case you pass on the right.
questions.question: You pass on the left when the vehicle ahead has moved to the centre of the road to turn right and when overtaking a streetcar (tram).

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 2(4) you must not increase speed until the overtaking is finished, and you move as far left as you can and give way.
questions.question: When you are being overtaken and there is not enough room, it is best to speed up so that the other driver gives up.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 3(2) you also check that the oncoming side is clear when crossing over to overtake.
questions.question: Even when overtaking across onto the right-hand side, checking ahead and to the right rear is enough; the oncoming side need not be checked.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 4 you must not squeeze in alongside a vehicle travelling beside you.
questions.question: Squeezing in alongside a vehicle travelling beside you is no problem as long as you do not touch it.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 5(2) you stop or slow down beforehand and give way to oncoming vehicles.
questions.question: Where there is an obstruction ahead it is safer to get through first without slowing.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 2(1) you must overtake it on its left in that case.
questions.question: Even where the vehicle ahead has moved to the centre of the road to turn right, you overtake it on its right.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(2)(c) you must not overtake where it would obstruct oncoming vehicles.
questions.question: You saw an oncoming vehicle in the distance but thought you would make it if you accelerated, so you crossed onto the right-hand side and overtook.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 4(2). Where such a specification exists, you travel on the part the marking shows.
questions.question: When arrows or other road markings (標示) specify how to travel through a roundabout, you must follow what they specify.

questions.explanation: This is Article 37-2 paragraph 3 of the Road Traffic Act. On top of that you must proceed at the safest possible speed and in the safest possible manner for the state of the roundabout.
questions.question: When you are about to enter a roundabout or are travelling inside one, you must pay particular attention not only to vehicles travelling inside it but also to vehicles about to enter it and to pedestrians crossing the road at or immediately beside it.

questions.explanation: This is the definition in Article 4 paragraph 3 of the Road Traffic Act. A circular layout without that specification is not a roundabout.
questions.question: A roundabout is an intersection whose vehicle carriageway is circular and on which a road sign specifies that vehicles are to travel around that part clockwise.

questions.explanation: This is Article 35-2 paragraph 1 of the Road Traffic Act. That paragraph applies notwithstanding Article 34 paragraph 5, which sets out the two-step right turn, so no two-step right turn is made at a roundabout.
questions.question: When a general motorized bicycle (moped) turns right at a roundabout it does not use the two-step right turn; it keeps as far to the left of the road as it can and proceeds slowly (徐行) along the outer edge of the roundabout.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Article 37-2 paragraph 2 of the Road Traffic Act requires you to proceed slowly, not to come to a complete stop.
questions.question: When you are about to enter a roundabout you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) just before the stop line at the entrance.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. That is how you turn right at an intersection other than a roundabout; at a roundabout you keep to the left of the road and proceed slowly along the outer edge.
questions.question: When you turn right at a roundabout you first keep as close to the centre of the road as you can and proceed slowly (徐行) just inside the centre of the intersection.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Article 36 paragraph 1 of the Road Traffic Act, which gives priority to traffic from the left, does not apply at a roundabout; priority belongs to vehicles already travelling inside it.
questions.question: Inside a roundabout you must not obstruct the progress of a vehicle coming from your left.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. The duty to proceed slowly in Article 37-2 paragraph 2 of the Road Traffic Act has no exception for a roundabout that happens to be empty.
questions.question: Even when you are about to enter a roundabout, you need not proceed slowly (徐行) once you have confirmed that there is no vehicle inside it.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Article 37-2 paragraph 3 of the Road Traffic Act also requires particular attention to vehicles about to enter and to pedestrians crossing the road at or immediately beside the roundabout.
questions.question: The only traffic you have to pay particular attention to when travelling through a roundabout is the vehicles already inside it.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Article 36 paragraph 2 of the Road Traffic Act, which gives priority by road width, does not apply at a roundabout; whatever the widths, priority belongs to vehicles already travelling inside it.
questions.question: A roundabout is an intersection without traffic control, so a vehicle entering from the wider road has priority.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(1). Keeping left also stops you drawing in a bicycle alongside.
questions.question: To turn left at an intersection you must first keep as far to the left of the road as you can and proceed slowly (徐行) along the edge of the intersection.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(2). A general motorized bicycle (moped) making a two-step right turn is an exception.
questions.question: To turn right at an intersection you must first keep as close to the centre of the road as you can and proceed slowly (徐行) just inside the centre of the intersection.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(3). On a one-way road there is no oncoming traffic, so you keep right.
questions.question: To turn right from a one-way road you first keep to the right edge of the road and proceed slowly (徐行) inside the centre of the intersection.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(4). A specification by marking overrides the general method of turning.
questions.question: Where arrows or other road markings specify how to turn, you must follow that specification.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(5). The same goes for streetcars (trams).
questions.question: When you are turning right and there are vehicles going straight on or turning left at that intersection, you must not obstruct them even if your own vehicle entered the intersection first.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 1(1). Intersections and their surroundings are where accidents happen most.
questions.question: When entering an intersection or travelling inside one you must proceed at the safest possible speed and in the safest possible manner for its state, with an eye on turning vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 1(1). A two-wheeler is small, and its speed and distance are hard to judge.
questions.question: When you are about to turn right, a two-wheeled vehicle coming straight on in the oncoming lane can be hard to see, so take particular care.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 1(3). The inner wheel difference is the gap between the paths of the front and rear wheels in a turn.
questions.question: A turning vehicle has an inner wheel difference, and a large vehicle in particular has a big one and poor visibility to its left rear, so take care not to draw in pedestrians or bicycles on your left.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(2). In a two-step right turn it keeps to the left edge and goes straight to the far side of the intersection.
questions.question: A general motorized bicycle (moped) making a two-step right turn does not need to move to the centre of the road.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 items 2(1) and 2(2). What differs is where you position the vehicle beforehand.
questions.question: Turning left and turning right at an intersection have this in common: both must be done proceeding slowly (徐行).

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(1) you keep as far to the left of the road as you can to turn left.
questions.question: To turn left at an intersection you first keep as close to the centre of the road as you can.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(5) you must not obstruct vehicles going straight on or turning left, even if you entered first.
questions.question: When turning right, you may turn ahead of oncoming vehicles going straight if your own vehicle entered the intersection first.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(3) you keep to the right edge of the road when turning right from a one-way road.
questions.question: To turn right from a one-way road you first move to the centre of the road.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(4) you must follow the specification where one exists.
questions.question: Even where arrows or other markings specify how to turn, you need not follow them when traffic is light.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 1(3) it is the rear wheels that run inside the front ones.
questions.question: The inner wheel difference is the gap between the paths of the front and rear wheels caused by the front wheels running inside the rear ones in a turn.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(1) you must also proceed slowly along the edge of the intersection.
questions.question: To turn left at an intersection it is enough to move to the left edge beforehand; proceeding slowly (徐行) is not required.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(2) a general motorized bicycle (moped) making a two-step right turn uses a different method.
questions.question: Every vehicle about to turn right at an intersection must first keep as close to the centre of the road as it can.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 1(1) a two-wheeler coming straight on in that lane can be hard to see, so it needs particular care.
questions.question: When turning right at an intersection it is enough to watch for cars in the oncoming lane.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(5) you must not obstruct vehicles going straight on, and a two-wheeler's speed is hard to judge.
questions.question: Turning right at an intersection you saw a two-wheeler coming straight on in the oncoming lane, but it looked small and slow, so you turned first.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(1), keeping as far left as you can beforehand is what stops a bicycle being drawn in.
questions.question: When turning left at an intersection it is best to leave the left edge of the road clear beforehand so that bicycles coming up behind can go first.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(6). Those two are the cases in which the assignment need not be followed.
questions.question: On a road with vehicle lanes where signs or markings assign lanes by the direction you will take at the intersection, you must travel in the assigned lane except when an emergency vehicle is approaching or road works and the like leave no alternative.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(7). It is the restriction imposed by the Proceed only in designated directions sign.
questions.question: At an intersection where a sign specifies the directions you may take, such as straight on or left, you must go only in the specified direction.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(8). The duty to give way is not owed at the cost of creating danger.
questions.question: When the vehicle ahead signals that it is changing course in order to turn or for a similar reason, you must not obstruct that change, except where avoiding it would take sudden braking or sudden steering.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(9). The same goes for a pedestrian crossing or railway crossing where you might be unable to move on.
questions.question: Where congestion ahead might leave you stopped inside the intersection and obstructing traffic from the crossing direction, you must not enter the intersection even on a green light.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(9). The rule keeps emergency vehicles free to come and go.
questions.question: At a place marked as a No stopping zone, such as in front of a police or fire station, you must not enter it when you might be left unable to move on.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 3(1). The same applies to streetcars (trams).
questions.question: At an intersection without traffic control, where the crossing road is a priority road or is clearly wider, you must proceed slowly (徐行) and must not obstruct vehicles travelling on it.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 3(2). This is the rule giving priority to traffic from the left.
questions.question: At an intersection of roads of similar width you must not obstruct a streetcar (tram) or a vehicle coming from your left.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 3(3). The same applies where a flashing red light faces you.
questions.question: Where the Stop sign stands you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) just before the stop line, or just before the intersection where there is none, and must not obstruct vehicles on the crossing road.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 3(4). A flashing red light calls for a complete stop (一時停止).
questions.question: Where a flashing yellow light faces you, you may proceed with care for other traffic.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(6). At such an intersection the two-step method overrides the lane assignment.
questions.question: At an intersection where a two-step right turn is required, a general motorized bicycle (moped) about to turn must keep to the left edge of the road whatever the lane assignment says.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(9) you must not enter even on green where you might obstruct traffic from the crossing direction.
questions.question: As long as the light is green you may enter the intersection even if congestion ahead might leave you stopped inside it.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 3(2) it is the vehicle coming from your left that you must not obstruct.
questions.question: At an intersection of roads of similar width you must not obstruct a vehicle coming from your right.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 3(1) you must proceed slowly as well as not obstructing vehicles on that road.
questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection where the crossing road is a priority road, it is enough not to obstruct its traffic; proceeding slowly (徐行) is not required.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 3(3) you must both stop and refrain from obstructing vehicles on the crossing road.
questions.question: Where the Stop sign stands, you may go ahead of vehicles on the crossing road as long as you have come to a complete stop (一時停止).

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(6) an approaching emergency vehicle and road works that leave no alternative are exceptions.
questions.question: Where signs or markings assign lanes by the direction you will take at the intersection, you must follow that assignment in every case.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(7) you may go only in the specified direction.
questions.question: Even at an intersection where a sign specifies the direction, you may take another direction when the specified one is jammed ahead.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 3(4) a flashing yellow light lets you proceed with care for other traffic.
questions.question: Where a flashing yellow light faces you, you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) at the stopping position.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(8) the case where avoiding it would take sudden braking or sudden steering is an exception.
questions.question: When the vehicle ahead signals a change of course, you must never obstruct it, in any circumstances.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(9) you must not enter even on green where you might be left stopped inside the intersection.
questions.question: Because the light turned green you entered the intersection although you could see it was filled with cars beyond, and ended up stopped in front of the crossing traffic.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 3(1) you must proceed slowly (徐行) there and must not obstruct vehicles on the crossing road.
questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection you may go first if you reached it first, even where the crossing road is clearly wider.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(5). That holds even if your own vehicle entered the intersection first.
questions.question: When you are turning right and a streetcar (tram) is going straight on or turning left at that intersection, you must not obstruct it either.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 1(2). It is a rule shared with other intersections.
questions.question: When entering or travelling inside a roundabout you must also proceed at the safest possible speed and in the safest possible manner for the situation.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(9). The same goes for an intersection and for a place marked as a No stopping zone.
questions.question: Where you might be left unable to move on at a pedestrian crossing or railway crossing, you must not enter it.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 4(2). Where there is none, you proceed slowly (徐行) along the outer edge.
questions.question: Where arrows or other markings specify how to travel through a roundabout when turning, going straight on or making a U-turn, you must follow that specification.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 3(3). You must then not obstruct vehicles travelling on the crossing road.
questions.question: Where a flashing red light faces you, you come to a complete stop (一時停止) just before the stop line, as you would at a Stop sign.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 1(3). The same goes for specified small motorized bicycles.
questions.question: A large vehicle has a big inner wheel difference and poor visibility to its left rear, so take particular care not to draw in pedestrians or bicycles on your left.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(6). The same goes where road works or the like leave no alternative.
questions.question: Even on a road where lanes are assigned by the direction you will take at the intersection, you may depart from the assignment when an emergency vehicle approaches.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 4(3). Vehicles are not the only traffic you must not obstruct.
questions.question: When about to enter a roundabout you must proceed slowly (徐行) and must not obstruct a streetcar (tram) travelling inside it either.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(8). The case where avoiding it would take sudden braking or steering is an exception.
questions.question: When the vehicle ahead signals a change of course in order to use the lane assigned to it, you must not obstruct that change either.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(7). You may go only in the specified direction.
questions.question: At an intersection where a sign permits only going straight on, you may not turn left either.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(5) you must not obstruct vehicles turning left or streetcars (trams) either.
questions.question: When turning right, the only traffic you must not obstruct is vehicles going straight on at that intersection.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(9) you must not enter a pedestrian crossing or railway crossing either where you might be left unable to move on.
questions.question: Even where you might be left unable to move on at a pedestrian crossing, you may enter as long as it is not inside an intersection.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 3(3) a flashing red light calls for a complete stop (一時停止) just before the stop line.
questions.question: Where a flashing red light faces you it is enough to proceed slowly (徐行).

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 4(2) you must follow a specification given by a marking.
questions.question: At a roundabout you need not follow arrows or other markings so long as you proceed slowly (徐行) along the outer edge.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(6) the cases in which you need not follow it are an approaching emergency vehicle and road works that leave no alternative.
questions.question: You need not follow the lane assignment at an intersection when traffic is congested.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 1(3) any vehicle has an inner wheel difference when turning; it is simply larger on a large vehicle.
questions.question: Only large vehicles have an inner wheel difference; it is not an issue for ordinary cars.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(7) you may go only in the specified direction.
questions.question: Even at an intersection where a sign specifies the direction, you may go another way if no other vehicle is doing so.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 4(3) you must not obstruct vehicles or streetcars travelling inside the roundabout.
questions.question: When about to enter a roundabout, the only traffic you must not obstruct is vehicles; streetcars (trams) are not included.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(9) you must not enter where you might be left unable to move on.
questions.question: At a No stopping zone in front of a police station you drove in on a green light although you were likely to end up stopped in it.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 1(1) they are where accidents happen most, and you proceed at the safest possible speed and in the safest possible manner.
questions.question: Intersections and their surroundings are places where accidents are rare, so you may drive through at your usual speed.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(2). The step exists to stop you hitting the wrong pedal.
questions.question: Before starting the engine of an automatic vehicle you press the brake pedal to feel where it is and also look to check where the accelerator pedal is.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(2). Without checking the lever the car may move as soon as it starts.
questions.question: In an automatic vehicle you confirm that the handbrake is on and the selector lever is in P, then press the brake pedal and start the engine.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(3). The higher the revolutions, the stronger the creep.
questions.question: Just after the engine starts and while the air conditioning is running, engine revolutions are higher and the car may leap forward, so press the brake pedal especially firmly.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(4). While stopped you keep the brake pedal firmly pressed and also apply the handbrake as a precaution.
questions.question: When you stop at an intersection or the like and the wait looks like being long, put the selector into N.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(4). This is the creep phenomenon (クリープ), and it causes unexpected collisions.
questions.question: Unless the brake pedal is kept firmly pressed, the car can start creeping forward without the accelerator being touched.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(5). Do not select P before the car has come to a complete halt.
questions.question: To park, you apply the handbrake firmly with the brake pedal still pressed and only then put the selector into P.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 2. Drive without putting too much faith in the technology.
questions.question: The systems of an advanced safety vehicle (ASV) have limits, such as failing to work properly above a certain speed.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 2. It differs from an automated driving device, which takes the driver's operations over.
questions.question: An advanced safety vehicle (ASV) carries driver-assistance technology that assumes the driver keeps checking the surroundings and performing the necessary operations.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(5) you are told not to select P before the car has fully stopped.
questions.question: When parking you may put the selector into P before the car has come to a complete halt.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(1) you need to understand the basics of driving an automatic and operate it accurately.
questions.question: Because an automatic vehicle needs no clutch work and is easy to drive, you may treat it casually.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(4), unless the brake pedal is kept firmly pressed the car can creep forward.
questions.question: While stopped at an intersection the car will not move unless you touch the accelerator.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(3) you select R to reverse.
questions.question: To reverse an automatic vehicle you put the selector into D.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 2 an ASV is assistance technology that assumes the driver keeps checking the surroundings.
questions.question: Because an advanced safety vehicle (ASV) has collision-mitigation braking, you may leave watching the road ahead to the system.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(4) you put the selector into N when the wait looks like being long.
questions.question: When you stop at an intersection and the wait looks like being long, you put the selector into P.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(4) you keep the brake pedal firmly pressed while stopped and apply the handbrake as a precaution.
questions.question: The wait at the lights was long, so you took your foot off the brake pedal of your automatic and the car began creeping forward.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(3) working the selector without pressing the brake pedal firmly can make the car leap forward.
questions.question: The only thing to watch for in an automatic vehicle is the creep phenomenon; there is no risk of it leaping forward.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 1(1). You open a window so that you can hear as well.
questions.question: Before crossing a railway crossing you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) just before it, or just before the stop line where there is one, and check that it is safe to left and right with your own eyes and ears.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 1(1). On a green light you may cross without stopping.
questions.question: Where a railway crossing has a traffic light, you may cross in accordance with that light.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 1(4). The fact that the vehicle ahead got across is no guarantee for you.
questions.question: Even when following the vehicle ahead across a railway crossing, you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) and check that it is safe.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 1(4). Stuck on the tracks, you have nowhere to go.
questions.question: Where congestion beyond the railway crossing means you might be unable to move on once inside it, you must not enter.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 1(5). If the engine dies on the tracks, getting out becomes difficult.
questions.question: To avoid stalling, you cross a railway crossing in one go in the low gear you started in, without changing gear.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 1(5). The road surface at the edge of a crossing is often broken up.
questions.question: Inside a railway crossing you keep slightly towards the centre so as not to drop a wheel off, while watching for pedestrians and oncoming vehicles.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 2. Both the warning and the removal are required.
questions.question: If your vehicle will not move on a railway crossing you must let the train driver know as fast as you can and also get the vehicle off the crossing.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 2(1). Where there is no such device you signal with a flare or the like.
questions.question: If your vehicle will not move on a crossing that has an alarm, use the push-button emergency alarm fitted to the alarm post or similar.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 1(3) you must not enter a crossing while the barrier is coming down.
questions.question: When the barrier has only just begun to come down you may enter, since you can get across if you hurry.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 1(2) another train can be approaching from the opposite direction right behind it.
questions.question: Once a train from one direction has finished passing, you may judge the crossing to be safe.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 1(1) you open a window and check with your ears as well as your eyes.
questions.question: Checking at a railway crossing is a matter of looking left and right with your own eyes, and that is enough.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 1(1), where the crossing has a traffic light you may cross in accordance with it.
questions.question: At a railway crossing you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) even where there is a traffic light.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 1(5) you keep slightly towards the centre to avoid dropping a wheel.
questions.question: Inside a railway crossing you keep as far to the left of the road as you can so as not to drop a wheel off.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 2 you must also get the vehicle off the crossing.
questions.question: If your vehicle will not move on a railway crossing, letting the train driver know is enough; you need not move the vehicle.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 1(4) you must not enter where you might be left unable to move on inside it.
questions.question: The far side of the railway crossing was jammed, but because the barrier was up you drove onto the crossing.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 2(3) you signal by burning something smoky nearby or in another such way.
questions.question: If your vehicle will not move on a railway crossing and you have used up your flares, there is no longer any way to warn the train.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 1(1). The sound of a train can reach you before the sight of it.
questions.question: You check that it is safe at a railway crossing with your own eyes and ears, opening a window and so on.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 2(2). Without flares, you burn something smoky or signal in another such way.
questions.question: If your vehicle will not move where there is no push-button emergency alarm, use the flares you carry to signal the train as early as you can.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 1(3) you must not enter while the alarm is sounding.
questions.question: You may enter a railway crossing while the alarm is sounding, as long as the barrier is not down.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 2 you must let the train driver know as fast as you can and get the vehicle off the crossing.
questions.question: If your vehicle will not move on a railway crossing, you may move it off the crossing first and tell the train afterwards.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 1(5) you keep slightly towards the centre so as not to drop a wheel, while watching for pedestrians and oncoming vehicles.
questions.question: The only thing to watch for inside a railway crossing is dropping a wheel; pedestrians and oncoming vehicles need not be considered.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 1(6). Which vehicle gives way depends on whether a pull-in bay is close by.
questions.question: On a hill the vehicle going down gives way to the one coming up, because moving off uphill is difficult, but where there is a pull-in bay nearby the vehicle going up uses that bay and waits.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 1(8). The vehicle on the cliff side is the one in greater danger of going over.
questions.question: On a road with a cliff on one side where a vehicle could fall, if oncoming vehicles cannot pass each other safely, the vehicle on the cliff side comes to a complete stop (一時停止) and gives way.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 2(4). The inner wheel difference is the gap between the paths of the front and rear wheels, because the rear wheels run inside the front ones in a turn.
questions.question: When you go round a bend or a curve, the inner wheel difference can draw in a pedestrian or a bicycle on the inside, or take the rear wheels off the shoulder of the road.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 1(6), where there is a pull-in bay nearby, even the vehicle going up uses that bay and waits.
questions.question: Since the vehicle going down a hill gives way to the one coming up, the vehicle going up never has to wait.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 2(5) you must not overtake the vehicle ahead at a bend or a curve.
questions.question: Even at a bend or a curve you may overtake the vehicle ahead once you have confirmed that nothing is coming the other way.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 1(4) you use a low gear to make good use of the engine brake and avoid using the foot brake too often.
questions.question: On a long descent it is best to leave the engine brake alone and use the foot brake repeatedly instead.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 2(3) asks you to watch out precisely because an oncoming vehicle may come across the centre of the road.
questions.question: At a bend or a curve, as long as you keep from crossing the centre of the road, an oncoming vehicle will never cross it either.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 1(1). The vehicle ahead may roll back into you.
questions.question: When stopping behind another vehicle on an uphill slope, do not get too close to it.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 1(2). Trying to move off on the clutch alone can fail and let the car roll back.
questions.question: When moving off on an uphill slope, use the handbrake as far as you can.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 1(5). On a descent you also make good use of the engine brake.
questions.question: On a downhill slope you pick up speed and the stopping distance grows, so keep a wider following distance.
