questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 1(9). In some cases the vehicle on the cliff side stops and gives way.
questions.question: On a mountain road the shoulder may be liable to give way, so take care not to move too close to it when passing an oncoming vehicle.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 2(3). Watch out, because an oncoming vehicle may come across the centre.
questions.question: At a bend or a curve, keep from crossing the centre of the road.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 1(1) the vehicle ahead may roll back into you, so you do not get too close.
questions.question: When stopping behind another vehicle on an uphill slope it is best to pull up as close as you can.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 1(2) you use the handbrake as far as you can. On the clutch alone the attempt can fail and the car roll back.
questions.question: It is better to move off on an uphill slope on the clutch alone, without the handbrake.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 1(5) you pick up speed and the stopping distance grows on a descent, so you keep a wider distance.
questions.question: On a downhill slope the vehicle ahead slows too, so a short following distance is fine.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 1(9) the shoulder on a mountain road may be liable to give way, so you take care not to move too close.
questions.question: When passing an oncoming vehicle on a mountain road, moving as close to the shoulder as possible is safe.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 1(3) you must not overtake near the crest of a hill.
questions.question: The vehicle ahead was slow near the crest of a hill, so you checked that nothing was coming the other way and overtook.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 2(2) you turn the wheel gently so as not to steer sharply.
questions.question: A curve is steadier if you swing the wheel sharply and get round in one go.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 2. A moped is no exception.
questions.question: You must not ride a large motorcycle, an ordinary motorcycle or a general motorized bicycle (moped) without wearing a safety helmet.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 2. The passenger's helmet is the rider's responsibility too.
questions.question: You must not ride a large or ordinary motorcycle carrying someone who is not wearing a safety helmet.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 1(1)(a). It is a gauge of whether the machine suits your build.
questions.question: Being able to put the machine on its centre stand easily on level ground is one of the things to check when choosing a motorcycle.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 1(1)(c). Start with a small machine and move up as your skill grows.
questions.question: Being able to wheel the machine in a complete figure of eight is one of the things to check when choosing a motorcycle.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 4(1). A moped may not carry a passenger whether or not it has a seat for one.
questions.question: You must not carry a passenger on a large or ordinary motorcycle that has no pillion seat, or on a general motorized bicycle (moped).

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 4(3). It turns on how long you have held the licence.
questions.question: Someone within one year of obtaining an ordinary motorcycle licence must not carry a passenger on an ordinary motorcycle.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 3. The same goes for a passenger.
questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, dress so as to leave as little of the body exposed as possible, and wear protectors where you can.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 3. What matters is being easy for other drivers to see.
questions.question: When riding at night, wear reflective clothing or a safety helmet with reflective material on it.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 4(2) the bar applies to someone within one year of obtaining the licence.
questions.question: Someone within three years of obtaining a large motorcycle licence must not carry a passenger on a large motorcycle.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 4(2) they may carry a passenger if they have held an ordinary motorcycle licence for a year or more.
questions.question: Someone within one year of obtaining a large motorcycle licence cannot carry a passenger on a large motorcycle.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 4 it is also prohibited on a machine with no pillion seat and where the rider has not held the licence long enough.
questions.question: Carrying a passenger is prohibited only when riding a general motorized bicycle (moped).

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 2 you must not ride carrying someone who is not wearing a safety helmet.
questions.question: Carrying someone without a helmet on the pillion is acceptable as long as the rider is wearing one.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 1(1) going straight to a large machine is dangerous however strong you are; you start with a small one.
questions.question: If you are confident in your strength you may start straight away on a large motorcycle.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 6 you also check the chain tension, the handlebars, the lights, the mirrors and the exhaust.
questions.question: A motorcycle check need only cover the brakes and the tyres.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 2 you must not ride a moped without a safety helmet.
questions.question: Because it was only as far as the convenience store nearby, you rode your general motorized bicycle (moped) without a safety helmet.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 2 you must wear it properly, with the chin strap securely fastened.
questions.question: A safety helmet is fine as long as it is on your head, even with the chin strap undone.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 5. A machine handles differently with a passenger aboard.
questions.question: Even where carrying a passenger is not prohibited, do so only once you are practised at riding alone.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 6(4). You check that it is neither too slack nor too tight.
questions.question: In checking a motorcycle you test the chain's slack by pressing its middle with a finger.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 3. Keep ample following distance and side clearance.
questions.question: A motorcycle is nimble, but you must not weave between vehicles, ride in zigzags, force an overtaking or cut in.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 3. Your feet also hold the machine up and work the brake and the gears.
questions.question: When riding a motorcycle you must not wear footwear that gets in the way, such as wooden clogs or sandals.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 3 item 2. Avoid braking, sudden acceleration and large steering movements.
questions.question: On mud or gravel you drop to a low gear to reduce speed and keep the speed steady with the throttle while holding your balance.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 3 item 3(2)(a). It then goes straight to the far side of the intersection on a green light, proceeding slowly (徐行), stops there and turns to face right.
questions.question: For a two-step right turn a general motorized bicycle (moped) first keeps as far to the left of the road as it can and signals the turn on reaching the point 30 metres before the near edge of the intersection.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 3 item 2(2) you avoid braking and sudden acceleration and hold a steady speed with the throttle.
questions.question: On mud or gravel it is best to brake repeatedly to keep the speed down as you go through.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 3 weaving between vehicles is extremely dangerous and must not be done.
questions.question: Because a motorcycle is nimble you may weave between vehicles when the traffic is jammed.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 3 item 3(2)(a) a two-step right turn cannot be made on a green arrow.
questions.question: A general motorized bicycle (moped) making a two-step right turn may still turn on a green arrow signal.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 3 item 1(1) you must slow down enough beforehand on the straight leading into the curve.
questions.question: You came to a curve on a motorcycle, entered it without slowing and braked partway round.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 3 you also watch for someone in a stopped car opening a door suddenly and for pedestrians stepping out from between vehicles.
questions.question: Riding past queued traffic on a motorcycle, the only thing to watch is what the vehicle ahead does.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 3 item 3(1). Moving suddenly from the left-hand lane to the right-hand one is extremely dangerous.
questions.question: When you are going to turn right on a wide road, move across to the right-turn lane gradually from well beforehand.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 3 item 3(1) you move across to the right-turn lane gradually from well beforehand.
questions.question: When turning right on a wide road it is best to swing across to the right-hand lane just before the intersection.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(5) together with Chapter 5 Section 3 item 2(2). You must give way to both the through traffic and the pedestrian.
questions.question: Turning right at an intersection you gave way to a vehicle going straight on in the oncoming lane, and then also gave way to a pedestrian about to use the crossing.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 2(3). Someone crossing from behind the stopped vehicle cannot be seen.
questions.question: A vehicle was stopped before the pedestrian crossing, so you came to a complete stop (一時停止) before passing it and moving ahead.
